text.en: A router's IPv4 routing table contains several routes that all match an incoming packet's destination address. Which route does the router use to forward the packet?
text.hi: Ek router ki IPv4 routing table mein kai routes hain jo sab ek incoming packet ke destination address se match karte hain. Router packet ko forward karne ke liye kaunsa route use karta hai?

explanation.en: Forwarding is always decided by the longest prefix match: among all routes whose prefix covers the destination, the one with the most bits in its mask wins. Administrative distance and metric are used earlier, when deciding which routes get INSTALLED in the table — not when choosing among different prefixes at forwarding time.
explanation.hi: Forwarding hamesha longest prefix match se decide hoti hai: jitne bhi routes ka prefix destination ko cover karta hai, unmein se jis route ke mask mein sabse zyada bits hain, wahi jeetta hai. Administrative distance aur metric pehle use hote hain, jab yeh decide hota hai ki kaunse routes table mein INSTALL honge — forwarding ke time alag-alag prefixes ke beech choose karte waqt nahi.

options.en: The route with the longest prefix length (most specific match)
options.hi: Sabse lambi prefix length wala route (most specific match)

options.en: The route with the lowest administrative distance, regardless of prefix length
options.hi: Sabse kam administrative distance wala route, prefix length chahe kuch bhi ho

options.en: The route with the lowest metric, regardless of prefix length
options.hi: Sabse kam metric wala route, prefix length chahe kuch bhi ho

options.en: The route that was installed in the table first
options.hi: Woh route jo table mein sabse pehle install hua tha

whyWrong.en: AD selects between different routing sources offering the SAME prefix; it is not compared across routes with different prefix lengths.
whyWrong.hi: AD un alag-alag routing sources ke beech choose karta hai jo SAME prefix offer kar rahe hain; alag prefix lengths wale routes ke beech AD compare nahi hota.

whyWrong.en: Metric compares routes to the same prefix learned by the same protocol; a /24 with a high metric still beats a /16 with a low metric.
whyWrong.hi: Metric sirf same protocol se seekhe gaye same prefix ke routes ko compare karta hai; high metric wala /24 bhi low metric wale /16 ko hara deta hai.

whyWrong.en: Installation order plays no role in path selection; the table is evaluated for the most specific match on every lookup.
whyWrong.hi: Install hone ka order path selection mein koi role nahi rakhta; har lookup par table mein most specific match dhoondha jaata hai.

text.en:
A routing table contains this entry:

O     10.16.32.0/24 [110/45] via 10.1.13.2, GigabitEthernet0/1

What does the value 110 represent?
text.hi:
Ek routing table mein yeh entry hai:

O     10.16.32.0/24 [110/45] via 10.1.13.2, GigabitEthernet0/1

Value 110 kya represent karti hai?

explanation.en: In the [X/Y] notation, X is the administrative distance and Y is the metric. 110 is OSPF's default AD (how trustworthy the source is), and 45 is the OSPF cost to reach 10.16.32.0/24. Memorize the AD ladder: connected 0, static 1, eBGP 20, EIGRP 90, OSPF 110, IS-IS 115, RIP 120.
explanation.hi: [X/Y] notation mein X administrative distance hai aur Y metric hai. 110 OSPF ka default AD hai (source kitna trustworthy hai), aur 45 10.16.32.0/24 tak pahunchne ki OSPF cost hai. AD ladder yaad kar lo: connected 0, static 1, eBGP 20, EIGRP 90, OSPF 110, IS-IS 115, RIP 120.

options.en: The OSPF cost to reach the network
options.hi: Network tak pahunchne ki OSPF cost

options.en: The administrative distance of the route source
options.hi: Route source ka administrative distance

options.en: The hop count to the destination
options.hi: Destination tak ka hop count

options.en: The OSPF process ID
options.hi: OSPF process ID

whyWrong.en: The cost (metric) is the second number, 45, not 110.
whyWrong.hi: Cost (metric) doosra number hai, yaani 45, 110 nahi.

whyWrong.en: OSPF does not use hop count as a metric, and neither number in brackets is a hop count for OSPF routes.
whyWrong.hi: OSPF hop count ko metric ki tarah use nahi karta, aur OSPF routes ke liye brackets ka koi bhi number hop count nahi hota.

whyWrong.en: The process ID is locally significant configuration and never appears in the [AD/metric] brackets.
whyWrong.hi: Process ID ek locally significant configuration hai aur [AD/metric] brackets mein kabhi nahi dikhta.

text.en:
A router's table shows:

C     192.168.1.0/24 is directly connected, GigabitEthernet0/0
L     192.168.1.1/32 is directly connected, GigabitEthernet0/0

What does the L entry represent?
text.hi:
Ek router ki table yeh dikhati hai:

C     192.168.1.0/24 is directly connected, GigabitEthernet0/0
L     192.168.1.1/32 is directly connected, GigabitEthernet0/0

L entry kya represent karti hai?

explanation.en: For every IPv4 address configured on an up interface, IOS installs two routes: a C (connected) route for the subnet, and an L (local) /32 route for the interface's own address. The local route lets the router recognize packets addressed to itself. Here 192.168.1.1 is the address on G0/0.
explanation.hi: Kisi up interface par configure kiye gaye har IPv4 address ke liye IOS do routes install karta hai: subnet ke liye ek C (connected) route, aur interface ke apne address ke liye ek L (local) /32 route. Local route ki wajah se router apne liye aaye packets pehchaan paata hai. Yahan 192.168.1.1 G0/0 ka address hai.

options.en: A host learned dynamically through ARP
options.hi: ARP ke through dynamically seekha gaya ek host

options.en: A local host route for the IP address configured on the router's own interface
options.hi: Router ke apne interface par configure kiye gaye IP address ka local host route

options.en: A loopback interface network
options.hi: Ek loopback interface network

options.en: A static host route added by an administrator
options.hi: Administrator ka add kiya hua static host route

whyWrong.en: ARP entries live in the ARP cache, not in the routing table; L routes come from the interface configuration.
whyWrong.hi: ARP entries ARP cache mein rehti hain, routing table mein nahi; L routes interface configuration se aate hain.

whyWrong.en: Loopback interfaces also generate C and L entries, but this L route points to GigabitEthernet0/0, a physical interface.
whyWrong.hi: Loopback interfaces bhi C aur L entries banate hain, lekin yeh L route GigabitEthernet0/0 ki taraf point karta hai, jo ek physical interface hai.

whyWrong.en: Static routes display code S; L routes are created automatically when the interface address is configured.
whyWrong.hi: Static routes code S dikhate hain; L routes interface address configure hote hi automatically ban jaate hain.

text.en: A router learns the prefix 192.168.50.0/24 from three sources at the same time: OSPF (metric 40), EIGRP (metric 312560), and RIP (metric 3). Which route is installed in the routing table?
text.hi: Ek router prefix 192.168.50.0/24 ek hi time par teen sources se seekhta hai: OSPF (metric 40), EIGRP (metric 312560), aur RIP (metric 3). Routing table mein kaunsa route install hoga?

explanation.en: When different protocols offer the exact same prefix, the router compares administrative distance, not metric: EIGRP 90 beats OSPF 110 and RIP 120, so the EIGRP route wins despite its large-looking metric. Metrics are only comparable within a single protocol — 312560 (EIGRP composite) and 3 (RIP hops) measure different things.
explanation.hi: Jab alag-alag protocols bilkul same prefix offer karte hain, toh router metric nahi, administrative distance compare karta hai: EIGRP 90, OSPF 110 aur RIP 120 dono ko hara deta hai, isliye EIGRP route jeetta hai, chahe uska metric bada dikhe. Metrics sirf ek hi protocol ke andar comparable hote hain — 312560 (EIGRP composite) aur 3 (RIP hops) alag-alag cheezein measure karte hain.

options.en: The RIP route, because its metric of 3 is lowest
options.hi: RIP route, kyunki uska metric 3 sabse kam hai

options.en: The OSPF route, because OSPF is a link-state protocol
options.hi: OSPF route, kyunki OSPF ek link-state protocol hai

options.en: The EIGRP route, because EIGRP has the lowest administrative distance
options.hi: EIGRP route, kyunki EIGRP ka administrative distance sabse kam hai

options.en: All three routes are installed and traffic is load-balanced
options.hi: Teeno routes install hote hain aur traffic load-balance hota hai

whyWrong.en: Metrics from different protocols cannot be compared; RIP's hop count of 3 is not 'better' than EIGRP's 312560 — they are different units.
whyWrong.hi: Alag protocols ke metrics compare nahi ho sakte; RIP ka hop count 3 EIGRP ke 312560 se 'better' nahi hai — dono alag units hain.

whyWrong.en: Being link-state does not grant preference; OSPF's AD of 110 loses to EIGRP's 90.
whyWrong.hi: Link-state hone se koi preference nahi milti; OSPF ka AD 110 EIGRP ke 90 se haar jaata hai.

whyWrong.en: Only the route from the source with the lowest AD is installed for a given prefix; multi-source load balancing across protocols does not occur.
whyWrong.hi: Kisi prefix ke liye sirf sabse kam AD wale source ka route install hota hai; protocols ke beech multi-source load balancing nahi hoti.

text.en:
A routing table begins with:

Gateway of last resort is 203.0.113.1 to network 0.0.0.0

S*    0.0.0.0/0 [1/0] via 203.0.113.1

What does the asterisk after the S indicate?
text.hi:
Ek routing table aise shuru hoti hai:

Gateway of last resort is 203.0.113.1 to network 0.0.0.0

S*    0.0.0.0/0 [1/0] via 203.0.113.1

S ke baad wala asterisk kya batata hai?

explanation.en: The asterisk flags a candidate default route. Because this 0.0.0.0/0 static route is installed, the router sets its gateway of last resort to 203.0.113.1 — the next hop used for any destination that matches no more specific route.
explanation.hi: Asterisk ek candidate default route ko mark karta hai. Kyunki yeh 0.0.0.0/0 static route install hai, router apna gateway of last resort 203.0.113.1 set kar deta hai — yeh woh next hop hai jo har us destination ke liye use hota hai jo kisi more specific route se match nahi karta.

options.en: The route is a candidate default route
options.hi: Yeh route ek candidate default route hai

options.en: The route has the best metric of all static routes
options.hi: Is route ka metric saare static routes mein sabse best hai

options.en: The route is being advertised to neighboring routers
options.hi: Yeh route neighboring routers ko advertise ho raha hai

options.en: The route is permanently installed and cannot be removed
options.hi: Yeh route permanently installed hai aur remove nahi ho sakta

whyWrong.en: The asterisk says nothing about metric; a static route's metric is always shown as 0.
whyWrong.hi: Asterisk metric ke baare mein kuch nahi batata; static route ka metric hamesha 0 dikhaya jaata hai.

whyWrong.en: Static routes are not advertised to neighbors unless a routing protocol is explicitly configured to originate or redistribute them.
whyWrong.hi: Static routes neighbors ko advertise nahi hote jab tak koi routing protocol explicitly unhe originate ya redistribute karne ke liye configure na ho.

whyWrong.en: Removing the ip route command (or losing the next hop) removes the route; the asterisk does not make it permanent.
whyWrong.hi: ip route command hata do (ya next hop chala jaaye) toh route hat jaata hai; asterisk usse permanent nahi banata.

text.en:
A router has this routing table:

S     10.0.0.0/8 [1/0] via 203.0.113.2
O     10.16.0.0/16 [110/20] via 10.1.12.2, GigabitEthernet0/0
O     10.16.32.0/24 [110/45] via 10.1.13.2, GigabitEthernet0/1
S*    0.0.0.0/0 [1/0] via 203.0.113.1

Which next hop is used for a packet destined to 10.16.32.9?
text.hi:
Ek router ki routing table yeh hai:

S     10.0.0.0/8 [1/0] via 203.0.113.2
O     10.16.0.0/16 [110/20] via 10.1.12.2, GigabitEthernet0/0
O     10.16.32.0/24 [110/45] via 10.1.13.2, GigabitEthernet0/1
S*    0.0.0.0/0 [1/0] via 203.0.113.1

10.16.32.9 destination wale packet ke liye kaunsa next hop use hoga?

explanation.en: 10.16.32.9 falls inside 10.16.32.0/24 (which covers 10.16.32.0 through 10.16.32.255), and /24 is the longest matching prefix, so the packet goes via 10.1.13.2. The /24's higher metric (45 versus 20) is irrelevant — metric never overrides a longer prefix.
explanation.hi: 10.16.32.9, 10.16.32.0/24 ke andar aata hai (jo 10.16.32.0 se 10.16.32.255 tak cover karta hai), aur /24 sabse lamba matching prefix hai, isliye packet 10.1.13.2 ke through jaata hai. /24 ka zyada metric (45 vs 20) koi matter nahi karta — metric kabhi bhi longer prefix ko override nahi karta.

whyWrong.en: 10.0.0.0/8 matches, but /8 is the shortest of the matching prefixes and loses to the /24.
whyWrong.hi: 10.0.0.0/8 match karta hai, lekin matching prefixes mein /8 sabse chhota hai aur /24 se haar jaata hai.

whyWrong.en: 10.16.0.0/16 matches, but the /24 route is more specific and is preferred despite its higher metric.
whyWrong.hi: 10.16.0.0/16 match karta hai, lekin /24 route zyada specific hai aur zyada metric ke bawajood prefer hota hai.

whyWrong.en: The default route is used only when no other route matches; here three more specific routes match.
whyWrong.hi: Default route sirf tab use hota hai jab koi aur route match na kare; yahan teen more specific routes match kar rahe hain.

text.en:
A router has this routing table:

S     10.0.0.0/8 [1/0] via 203.0.113.2
O     10.16.0.0/16 [110/20] via 10.1.12.2, GigabitEthernet0/0
O     10.16.32.0/24 [110/45] via 10.1.13.2, GigabitEthernet0/1
S*    0.0.0.0/0 [1/0] via 203.0.113.1

Which next hop is used for a packet destined to 10.16.47.10?
text.hi:
Ek router ki routing table yeh hai:

S     10.0.0.0/8 [1/0] via 203.0.113.2
O     10.16.0.0/16 [110/20] via 10.1.12.2, GigabitEthernet0/0
O     10.16.32.0/24 [110/45] via 10.1.13.2, GigabitEthernet0/1
S*    0.0.0.0/0 [1/0] via 203.0.113.1

10.16.47.10 destination wale packet ke liye kaunsa next hop use hoga?

explanation.en: 10.16.47.10 is NOT inside 10.16.32.0/24 (that route only covers addresses whose third octet is 32). It does fall inside 10.16.0.0/16, which is more specific than 10.0.0.0/8, so the packet is forwarded via 10.1.12.2.
explanation.hi: 10.16.47.10, 10.16.32.0/24 ke andar NAHI hai (woh route sirf un addresses ko cover karta hai jinka third octet 32 hai). Lekin yeh 10.16.0.0/16 ke andar aata hai, jo 10.0.0.0/8 se zyada specific hai, isliye packet 10.1.12.2 ke through forward hota hai.

whyWrong.en: 10.0.0.0/8 matches but is less specific than the /16; longest match wins.
whyWrong.hi: 10.0.0.0/8 match karta hai lekin /16 se kam specific hai; longest match jeetta hai.

whyWrong.en: 10.16.32.0/24 covers only 10.16.32.0 through 10.16.32.255; the destination's third octet is 47, so this route does not match at all.
whyWrong.hi: 10.16.32.0/24 sirf 10.16.32.0 se 10.16.32.255 tak cover karta hai; destination ka third octet 47 hai, isliye yeh route match hi nahi karta.

whyWrong.en: A more specific route (the /16) matches, so the default route is not consulted.
whyWrong.hi: Ek more specific route (/16) match kar raha hai, isliye default route dekha hi nahi jaata.

text.hi:
Ek router ki routing table yeh hai:

O     172.20.16.0/20 [110/30] via 10.0.0.6
O     172.20.24.0/22 [110/20] via 10.0.0.10
O     172.20.26.0/23 [110/50] via 10.0.0.14
S*    0.0.0.0/0 [1/0] via 10.0.0.2

172.20.27.133 destination wale packet ke liye kaunsa next hop use hoga?

explanation.en: Work out each range: 172.20.16.0/20 covers 172.20.16.0-172.20.31.255; 172.20.24.0/22 covers 172.20.24.0-172.20.27.255; 172.20.26.0/23 covers 172.20.26.0-172.20.27.255. The destination 172.20.27.133 sits inside all three, so the longest prefix (/23) wins and the packet goes via 10.0.0.14 — even though that route has the worst metric (50).
explanation.hi: Har range nikalo: 172.20.16.0/20 cover karta hai 172.20.16.0-172.20.31.255; 172.20.24.0/22 cover karta hai 172.20.24.0-172.20.27.255; 172.20.26.0/23 cover karta hai 172.20.26.0-172.20.27.255. Destination 172.20.27.133 teeno ke andar hai, isliye longest prefix (/23) jeetta hai aur packet 10.0.0.14 ke through jaata hai — chahe us route ka metric sabse kharab (50) hai.

whyWrong.en: The /20 matches but is the least specific of the three matching routes.
whyWrong.hi: /20 match karta hai lekin teen matching routes mein sabse kam specific hai.

whyWrong.en: The /22 matches and has the best metric (20), but metric is never compared across different prefixes — the /23 is more specific.
whyWrong.hi: /22 match karta hai aur uska metric sabse best (20) hai, lekin alag prefixes ke beech metric kabhi compare nahi hota — /23 zyada specific hai.

whyWrong.en: The default route is only a fallback; three more specific routes cover this destination.
whyWrong.hi: Default route sirf fallback hai; is destination ko teen more specific routes cover kar rahe hain.

text.en: R1 is configured with ip route 0.0.0.0 0.0.0.0 203.0.113.1 and its table shows S* 0.0.0.0/0 [1/0]. R1 also receives a default route advertisement (0.0.0.0/0) from an OSPF neighbor, but that OSPF default never appears in the routing table. Why?
text.hi: R1 par ip route 0.0.0.0 0.0.0.0 203.0.113.1 configure hai aur uski table S* 0.0.0.0/0 [1/0] dikhati hai. R1 ko ek OSPF neighbor se bhi default route advertisement (0.0.0.0/0) milta hai, lekin woh OSPF default routing table mein kabhi nahi dikhta. Kyun?

explanation.en: Both sources offer the identical prefix 0.0.0.0/0, so the tie is broken by administrative distance before anything is installed: static AD 1 is lower (more trusted) than OSPF AD 110, so only the static default is installed. If the static route were removed, the OSPF default would immediately take its place.
explanation.hi: Dono sources bilkul same prefix 0.0.0.0/0 offer kar rahe hain, isliye kuch bhi install hone se pehle tie administrative distance se tootta hai: static AD 1, OSPF AD 110 se kam (zyada trusted) hai, isliye sirf static default install hota hai. Agar static route hata diya jaaye, toh OSPF default turant uski jagah le lega.

options.en: The static route was configured before OSPF converged, and older routes cannot be replaced
options.hi: Static route OSPF converge hone se pehle configure hua tha, aur purane routes replace nahi ho sakte

options.en: Both candidates are the same prefix (0.0.0.0/0), so administrative distance decides: static (1) beats OSPF (110)
options.hi: Dono candidates same prefix (0.0.0.0/0) hain, isliye administrative distance decide karta hai: static (1) OSPF (110) ko hara deta hai

options.en: Longest prefix match prefers static routes over OSPF routes
options.hi: Longest prefix match static routes ko OSPF routes par prefer karta hai

options.en: OSPF cannot carry a default route in its advertisements
options.hi: OSPF apne advertisements mein default route carry nahi kar sakta

whyWrong.en: Age and configuration order never protect a route; if a lower-AD source appears, it replaces the installed route for that prefix.
whyWrong.hi: Age aur configuration order kabhi route ko protect nahi karte; agar kam AD wala source aata hai, toh woh us prefix ke installed route ko replace kar deta hai.

whyWrong.en: Longest prefix match compares prefix lengths at forwarding time; here both prefixes are /0, so prefix length cannot break the tie.
whyWrong.hi: Longest prefix match forwarding ke time prefix lengths compare karta hai; yahan dono prefixes /0 hain, isliye prefix length tie nahi tod sakti.

whyWrong.en: OSPF can advertise a default route (typically via default-information originate on another router) — R1 is in fact receiving one.
whyWrong.hi: OSPF default route advertise kar sakta hai (aam taur par kisi doosre router par default-information originate se) — R1 ko asal mein ek mil bhi raha hai.

text.en: Which THREE statements about IPv4 route selection are true? (Choose three)
text.hi: IPv4 route selection ke baare mein kaunse TEEN statements sahi hain? (Teen choose karo)

explanation.en: The three-step logic: (1) forwarding uses the longest prefix match among installed routes; (2) when sources compete to install the SAME prefix, the lowest AD wins (connected 0, static 1, eBGP 20, EIGRP 90, OSPF 110, IS-IS 115, RIP 120); (3) within one protocol, the lowest metric wins. Metrics from different protocols measure different things and are never compared to each other.
explanation.hi: Teen-step logic: (1) forwarding installed routes mein longest prefix match use karti hai; (2) jab sources SAME prefix install karne ke liye compete karte hain, toh sabse kam AD jeetta hai (connected 0, static 1, eBGP 20, EIGRP 90, OSPF 110, IS-IS 115, RIP 120); (3) ek protocol ke andar sabse kam metric jeetta hai. Alag protocols ke metrics alag cheezein measure karte hain aur ek doosre se kabhi compare nahi hote.

options.en: At forwarding time, the longest matching prefix is preferred no matter which protocol supplied the route
options.hi: Forwarding ke time longest matching prefix prefer hota hai, chahe route kisi bhi protocol ne diya ho

options.en: Administrative distance decides which source's route is installed when two sources offer the identical prefix
options.hi: Jab do sources bilkul same prefix offer karte hain, toh administrative distance decide karta hai ki kis source ka route install hoga

options.en: Metric compares alternative routes to the same prefix learned by the same protocol
options.hi: Metric same protocol se seekhe gaye same prefix ke alternative routes ko compare karta hai

options.en: A route with a lower metric is always preferred over a route with a longer prefix
options.hi: Kam metric wala route hamesha longer prefix wale route par prefer hota hai

options.en: OSPF cost and EIGRP metric can be compared directly to select the best path
options.hi: Best path choose karne ke liye OSPF cost aur EIGRP metric ko directly compare kiya ja sakta hai

whyWrong.en: Prefix length is evaluated first at forwarding time; a /28 with metric 1000 still beats a /24 with metric 1 for destinations inside the /28.
whyWrong.hi: Forwarding ke time prefix length pehle evaluate hoti hai; /28 ke andar wale destinations ke liye metric 1000 wala /28 bhi metric 1 wale /24 ko hara deta hai.

whyWrong.en: OSPF cost is bandwidth-derived and EIGRP's composite uses bandwidth plus delay on a different scale — they are incomparable units, which is exactly why AD exists.
whyWrong.hi: OSPF cost bandwidth se nikalti hai aur EIGRP ka composite bandwidth plus delay ek alag scale par use karta hai — yeh incomparable units hain, aur isi wajah se AD exist karta hai.

text.en: Which TWO route sources have a lower (more trusted) default administrative distance than OSPF? (Choose two)
text.hi: Kaunse DO route sources ka default administrative distance OSPF se kam (zyada trusted) hai? (Do choose karo)

explanation.en: OSPF's default AD is 110. External BGP (20) and internal EIGRP (90) are both lower, so they would be preferred over OSPF for the same prefix. IS-IS (115) and RIP (120) are higher, so OSPF beats them. Full ladder: connected 0, static 1, eBGP 20, EIGRP 90, OSPF 110, IS-IS 115, RIP 120.
explanation.hi: OSPF ka default AD 110 hai. External BGP (20) aur internal EIGRP (90) dono kam hain, isliye same prefix ke liye yeh OSPF par prefer honge. IS-IS (115) aur RIP (120) zyada hain, isliye OSPF unhe hara deta hai. Poori ladder: connected 0, static 1, eBGP 20, EIGRP 90, OSPF 110, IS-IS 115, RIP 120.

options.en: External BGP
options.hi: External BGP

options.en: EIGRP (internal)
options.hi: EIGRP (internal)

options.en: IS-IS
options.hi: IS-IS

options.en: RIP
options.hi: RIP

whyWrong.en: IS-IS has AD 115, which is higher (less trusted) than OSPF's 110.
whyWrong.hi: IS-IS ka AD 115 hai, jo OSPF ke 110 se zyada (kam trusted) hai.

whyWrong.en: RIP has AD 120, the least trusted of the common interior protocols.
whyWrong.hi: RIP ka AD 120 hai, common interior protocols mein sabse kam trusted.

text.en: Match each route source to its default administrative distance.
text.hi: Har route source ko uske default administrative distance se match karo.

explanation.en: Administrative distance ranks the trustworthiness of route sources; the lowest AD wins when the same prefix is offered by multiple sources. Connected 0, static 1, eBGP 20, EIGRP 90, OSPF 110, IS-IS 115, RIP 120 — the CCNA expects these cold.
explanation.hi: Administrative distance route sources ki trustworthiness ko rank karta hai; jab same prefix multiple sources se aata hai toh sabse kam AD jeetta hai. Connected 0, static 1, eBGP 20, EIGRP 90, OSPF 110, IS-IS 115, RIP 120 — CCNA mein yeh sab zubaani yaad hone chahiye.

text.en: Type the privileged EXEC command that displays the router's complete IPv4 routing table.
text.hi: Woh privileged EXEC command type karo jo router ki poori IPv4 routing table display karta hai.

explanation.en: show ip route lists every installed IPv4 route with its code (L local, C connected, S static, O OSPF, D EIGRP, R RIP, B BGP), the [AD/metric] pair, the next hop, and the exit interface. It is the first command in almost every routing troubleshooting workflow.
explanation.hi: show ip route har installed IPv4 route ko list karta hai, uske code ke saath (L local, C connected, S static, O OSPF, D EIGRP, R RIP, B BGP), [AD/metric] pair, next hop, aur exit interface. Lagbhag har routing troubleshooting workflow ka yeh pehla command hai.

text.en: Which command configures a static route to the 192.168.30.0/24 network through next-hop 10.1.1.2?
text.hi: Kaunsa command 192.168.30.0/24 network ke liye next-hop 10.1.1.2 ke through static route configure karta hai?

explanation.en: The IPv4 static route syntax is: ip route network subnet-mask next-hop (or exit-interface). The mask is a normal subnet mask, so /24 is written 255.255.255.0, and the destination network comes before the next hop.
explanation.hi: IPv4 static route ka syntax hai: ip route network subnet-mask next-hop (ya exit-interface). Mask ek normal subnet mask hota hai, isliye /24 ko 255.255.255.0 likhte hain, aur destination network next hop se pehle aata hai.

whyWrong.en: 0.0.0.255 is a wildcard mask — those belong in OSPF network statements and ACLs, not in ip route.
whyWrong.hi: 0.0.0.255 ek wildcard mask hai — yeh OSPF network statements aur ACLs mein use hota hai, ip route mein nahi.

whyWrong.en: The arguments are reversed: this tries to route TO 10.1.1.2 VIA 192.168.30.0.
whyWrong.hi: Arguments ulte hain: yeh 192.168.30.0 KE THROUGH 10.1.1.2 TAK route karne ki koshish karta hai.

whyWrong.en: IOS does not accept CIDR slash notation in the ip route command; the mask must be written in dotted decimal.
whyWrong.hi: IOS ip route command mein CIDR slash notation accept nahi karta; mask dotted decimal mein likhna zaroori hai.

text.en: Which command configures an IPv4 default static route that sends all otherwise-unmatched traffic to 203.0.113.1?
text.hi: Kaunsa command ek IPv4 default static route configure karta hai jo baaki saara unmatched traffic 203.0.113.1 ko bhejta hai?

explanation.en: The quad-zero route — network 0.0.0.0 with mask 0.0.0.0 — matches every IPv4 destination with a prefix length of 0, so it is used only when nothing more specific matches. It appears as S* and sets the gateway of last resort.
explanation.hi: Quad-zero route — network 0.0.0.0 mask 0.0.0.0 ke saath — prefix length 0 ke saath har IPv4 destination ko match karta hai, isliye yeh sirf tab use hota hai jab kuch aur specific match na kare. Yeh S* ki tarah dikhta hai aur gateway of last resort set karta hai.

options.en: ip default-gateway 203.0.113.1
options.hi: ip default-gateway 203.0.113.1

whyWrong.en: ip default-gateway is only used by devices that are NOT routing (for example a Layer 2 switch's management plane); a router with ip routing enabled ignores it.
whyWrong.hi: ip default-gateway sirf un devices par use hota hai jo routing NAHI kar rahe (jaise Layer 2 switch ka management plane); ip routing enabled router ise ignore kar deta hai.

whyWrong.en: Mask 255.255.255.255 with network 0.0.0.0 defines a host route to the single address 0.0.0.0, not a default route.
whyWrong.hi: Network 0.0.0.0 ke saath mask 255.255.255.255 sirf ek address 0.0.0.0 ka host route banata hai, default route nahi.

whyWrong.en: This would be a host route to the local broadcast address — meaningless as a default route.
whyWrong.hi: Yeh local broadcast address ka host route hoga — default route ki tarah iska koi matlab nahi.

text.en: What is the default administrative distance of an IPv4 static route configured with a next-hop address?
text.hi: Next-hop address ke saath configure kiye gaye IPv4 static route ka default administrative distance kya hai?

explanation.en: Static routes default to AD 1 — more trusted than every dynamic routing protocol and second only to connected routes (AD 0). That is why a static route normally overrides anything a protocol learns for the same prefix, and why floating statics must raise the AD on purpose.
explanation.hi: Static routes ka default AD 1 hota hai — har dynamic routing protocol se zyada trusted, aur sirf connected routes (AD 0) se peeche. Isi wajah se static route normally us prefix ke liye protocol ka seekha hua sab kuch override kar deta hai, aur isi wajah se floating statics mein AD jaan-boojh kar badhana padta hai.

whyWrong.en: AD 0 belongs to directly connected routes; a static route can never be more trusted than a connected interface.
whyWrong.hi: AD 0 directly connected routes ka hota hai; static route kabhi bhi connected interface se zyada trusted nahi ho sakta.

whyWrong.en: 5 is the AD of an EIGRP summary route, not a static route.
whyWrong.hi: 5 EIGRP summary route ka AD hai, static route ka nahi.

whyWrong.en: 110 is OSPF's default AD.
whyWrong.hi: 110 OSPF ka default AD hai.

text.en: R1 learns 10.50.0.0/16 through OSPF. You must add a static route through backup next-hop 172.16.1.2 that is used ONLY if the OSPF route disappears. Which command is correct?
text.hi: R1, 10.50.0.0/16 ko OSPF ke through seekhta hai. Tumhe backup next-hop 172.16.1.2 ke through ek static route add karna hai jo SIRF tab use ho jab OSPF route gayab ho jaaye. Kaunsa command sahi hai?

explanation.en: A floating static route must have an administrative distance HIGHER than the protocol it backs up. OSPF is 110, so any value above 110 (here 130) keeps the static route dormant while OSPF is healthy; when the OSPF route is withdrawn, the floating static is installed automatically.
explanation.hi: Floating static route ka administrative distance us protocol se ZYADA hona chahiye jiska woh backup hai. OSPF 110 hai, isliye 110 se upar koi bhi value (yahan 130) static route ko tab tak dormant rakhti hai jab tak OSPF healthy hai; jab OSPF route withdraw hota hai, floating static automatically install ho jaata hai.

whyWrong.en: AD 90 is lower than OSPF's 110, so the static would always win and OSPF would never be used — the opposite of a backup.
whyWrong.hi: AD 90 OSPF ke 110 se kam hai, isliye static hamesha jeetega aur OSPF kabhi use nahi hoga — backup ka bilkul ulta.

whyWrong.en: Equal AD does not make the route yield; it would compete with the OSPF route instead of quietly waiting as a backup. The AD must be strictly greater than 110.
whyWrong.hi: Equal AD se route peeche nahi hatta; woh backup ki tarah chupchaap wait karne ki jagah OSPF route se compete karega. AD strictly 110 se zyada hona chahiye.

whyWrong.en: With no AD specified the static defaults to 1 and permanently overrides the OSPF route.
whyWrong.hi: AD specify nahi kiya toh static default 1 par rehta hai aur OSPF route ko permanently override kar deta hai.

text.en: An engineer configures ip route 10.99.0.0 255.255.0.0 GigabitEthernet0/0 on a router whose G0/0 connects to a multi-access Ethernet segment. What is the main drawback of specifying only the exit interface here?
text.hi: Ek engineer ek router par ip route 10.99.0.0 255.255.0.0 GigabitEthernet0/0 configure karta hai jiska G0/0 ek multi-access Ethernet segment se connected hai. Yahan sirf exit interface specify karne ka main nuksaan kya hai?

explanation.en: With only an exit interface on Ethernet, the router believes the whole destination network is directly attached, so it sends an ARP request for each individual destination IP. Resolution then depends on the far-end router answering with proxy ARP — fragile and ARP-table-heavy. On multi-access links, configure a next-hop IP (or a fully specified route with both interface and next hop).
explanation.hi: Ethernet par sirf exit interface dene se router samajhta hai ki poora destination network directly attached hai, isliye woh har individual destination IP ke liye ARP request bhejta hai. Phir resolution is baat par depend karta hai ki doosri taraf ka router proxy ARP se reply kare — yeh fragile hai aur ARP table ko bhar deta hai. Multi-access links par next-hop IP configure karo (ya interface aur next hop dono ke saath fully specified route).

options.en: The route receives a higher administrative distance than a next-hop static route
options.hi: Route ko next-hop static route se zyada administrative distance milta hai

options.en: The router treats every destination in 10.99.0.0/16 as directly connected and must ARP for each destination address, which works only if the neighbor performs proxy ARP
options.hi: Router 10.99.0.0/16 ke har destination ko directly connected maanta hai aur har destination address ke liye ARP karna padta hai, jo sirf tab kaam karta hai jab neighbor proxy ARP kare

options.en: The route is ignored because Ethernet interfaces cannot be used in static routes
options.hi: Route ignore ho jaata hai kyunki Ethernet interfaces static routes mein use nahi ho sakte

options.en: The router forwards the traffic as broadcast frames on the segment
options.hi: Router traffic ko segment par broadcast frames ki tarah forward karta hai

whyWrong.en: Both forms default to AD 1; specifying the exit interface does not change the AD.
whyWrong.hi: Dono forms ka default AD 1 hai; exit interface specify karne se AD nahi badalta.

whyWrong.en: Ethernet interfaces are legal in static routes — the configuration is accepted, it just behaves poorly on multi-access media.
whyWrong.hi: Ethernet interfaces static routes mein legal hain — configuration accept hoti hai, bas multi-access media par yeh theek se behave nahi karti.

whyWrong.en: Traffic is still sent as unicast frames; the issue is how the next-hop MAC address gets resolved, not broadcasting.
whyWrong.hi: Traffic phir bhi unicast frames ki tarah jaata hai; issue yeh hai ki next-hop MAC address kaise resolve hota hai, broadcasting nahi.

text.en: Which command configures an IPv6 default static route through next-hop 2001:db8:12::2?
text.hi: Kaunsa command next-hop 2001:db8:12::2 ke through IPv6 default static route configure karta hai?

explanation.en: The IPv6 default route is ::/0 — all zeros with prefix length 0, the direct analog of IPv4's 0.0.0.0/0. It matches any IPv6 destination lacking a more specific route. Remember the router also needs ipv6 unicast-routing enabled to forward IPv6 traffic.
explanation.hi: IPv6 default route ::/0 hai — saare zeros aur prefix length 0, bilkul IPv4 ke 0.0.0.0/0 jaisa. Yeh har us IPv6 destination ko match karta hai jiska koi more specific route nahi hai. Yaad rakho, IPv6 traffic forward karne ke liye router par ipv6 unicast-routing bhi enabled hona chahiye.

whyWrong.en: 0.0.0.0/0 is IPv4 notation; the ipv6 route command requires an IPv6 prefix.
whyWrong.hi: 0.0.0.0/0 IPv4 notation hai; ipv6 route command ko IPv6 prefix chahiye.

whyWrong.en: ::/128 is a host route to the single unspecified address, not a default route — the prefix length must be 0.
whyWrong.hi: ::/128 single unspecified address ka host route hai, default route nahi — prefix length 0 honi chahiye.

whyWrong.en: IPv6 static routes use the ipv6 route command, not ip route.
whyWrong.hi: IPv6 static routes ipv6 route command use karte hain, ip route nahi.

text.en: An engineer wants to use a neighbor's link-local address as the next hop: ipv6 route 2001:db8:9::/64 fe80::2. Why must the command also include an exit interface (for example ipv6 route 2001:db8:9::/64 GigabitEthernet0/1 fe80::2)?
text.hi: Ek engineer neighbor ka link-local address next hop ki tarah use karna chahta hai: ipv6 route 2001:db8:9::/64 fe80::2. Command mein exit interface bhi kyun include karna zaroori hai (jaise ipv6 route 2001:db8:9::/64 GigabitEthernet0/1 fe80::2)?

explanation.en: Link-local addresses are only unique per link: fe80::2 could legitimately exist on every attached segment. A recursive lookup on fe80::2 is therefore ambiguous, so IOS requires the exit interface alongside a link-local next hop. This 'directly attached plus next hop' form is a fully specified static route.
explanation.hi: Link-local addresses sirf ek link par unique hote hain: fe80::2 har attached segment par legitimately exist kar sakta hai. Isliye fe80::2 par recursive lookup ambiguous hai, aur IOS link-local next hop ke saath exit interface maangta hai. Yeh 'directly attached plus next hop' form ek fully specified static route hai.

options.en: Link-local next hops are only valid on serial interfaces
options.hi: Link-local next hops sirf serial interfaces par valid hote hain

options.en: A link-local address is not unique in the routing domain — the same fe80:: address can exist on every link, so the router cannot determine which interface to use without being told
options.hi: Link-local address routing domain mein unique nahi hota — same fe80:: address har link par ho sakta hai, isliye bina bataye router decide nahi kar sakta ki kaunsa interface use kare

options.en: The exit interface lowers the administrative distance so the route can be installed
options.hi: Exit interface administrative distance kam kar deta hai taaki route install ho sake

options.en: IOS requires an exit interface on all IPv6 static routes
options.hi: IOS ko saare IPv6 static routes par exit interface chahiye

whyWrong.en: Link-local next hops are common on Ethernet; the media type is not the issue.
whyWrong.hi: Link-local next hops Ethernet par common hain; media type issue nahi hai.

whyWrong.en: The AD is 1 either way; the exit interface resolves ambiguity, it does not change trustworthiness.
whyWrong.hi: AD dono tarah 1 hi hai; exit interface ambiguity door karta hai, trustworthiness nahi badalta.

whyWrong.en: Routes using a global unicast next hop can be configured without an exit interface — the requirement applies specifically to link-local next hops.
whyWrong.hi: Global unicast next hop wale routes bina exit interface ke configure ho sakte hain — yeh requirement khaas taur par link-local next hops ke liye hai.

text.en: R1 was configured with ip route 10.60.0.0 255.255.0.0 GigabitEthernet0/1. The route appeared in show ip route yesterday but is missing today, although the command is still present in the running configuration. What is the most likely cause?
text.hi: R1 par ip route 10.60.0.0 255.255.0.0 GigabitEthernet0/1 configure kiya gaya tha. Kal yeh route show ip route mein dikh raha tha lekin aaj gayab hai, jabki command abhi bhi running configuration mein hai. Sabse likely cause kya hai?

explanation.en: A static route is only installed while it is usable: an exit-interface route requires that interface to be up/up, and a next-hop route requires the next hop to be resolvable. When G0/1 went down, IOS pulled the route from the table — while keeping the command in the configuration so the route returns automatically when the interface recovers.
explanation.hi: Static route sirf tab tak install rehta hai jab tak woh usable hai: exit-interface route ke liye woh interface up/up hona chahiye, aur next-hop route ke liye next hop resolvable hona chahiye. Jab G0/1 down hua, IOS ne route ko table se hata diya — lekin command configuration mein rakhi, taaki interface wapas aane par route automatically laut aaye.

options.en: Static routes age out of the table after 24 hours and must be refreshed
options.hi: Static routes 24 ghante baad table se age out ho jaate hain aur unhe refresh karna padta hai

options.en: GigabitEthernet0/1 is down, so IOS withdrew the static route from the table
options.hi: GigabitEthernet0/1 down hai, isliye IOS ne static route ko table se withdraw kar diya

options.en: An OSPF route to 10.60.0.0/16 replaced the static route
options.hi: 10.60.0.0/16 ke ek OSPF route ne static route ko replace kar diya

options.en: The ARP entry for the next hop expired
options.hi: Next hop ki ARP entry expire ho gayi

whyWrong.en: Static routes never age out; they stay installed as long as they remain valid and configured.
whyWrong.hi: Static routes kabhi age out nahi hote; jab tak woh valid aur configured hain, installed rehte hain.

whyWrong.en: OSPF's AD of 110 can never displace a static route at AD 1 for the same prefix.
whyWrong.hi: Same prefix ke liye OSPF ka AD 110 kabhi bhi AD 1 wale static route ko hata nahi sakta.

whyWrong.en: ARP expiry triggers a fresh ARP request during forwarding; it does not remove routes from the routing table.
whyWrong.hi: ARP expiry se forwarding ke time nayi ARP request jaati hai; isse routing table se routes remove nahi hote.

text.en:
R1's configuration contains:

ip route 10.50.0.0 255.255.0.0 172.16.1.2 130

show ip route displays only this entry for the prefix:

O     10.50.0.0/16 [110/30] via 10.1.12.2

Why is the static route absent from the routing table?
text.hi:
R1 ki configuration mein yeh hai:

ip route 10.50.0.0 255.255.0.0 172.16.1.2 130

show ip route is prefix ke liye sirf yeh entry dikhata hai:

O     10.50.0.0/16 [110/30] via 10.1.12.2

Static route routing table mein kyun nahi hai?

explanation.en: This is a floating static working exactly as designed. The routing table holds only the best (lowest-AD) route per prefix; with OSPF at 110 versus the static at 130, OSPF wins. The static route waits in the background and is installed the moment the OSPF route is withdrawn — providing an automatic backup path.
explanation.hi: Yeh floating static hai jo bilkul design ke hisaab se kaam kar raha hai. Routing table mein har prefix ka sirf best (lowest-AD) route hota hai; OSPF 110 vs static 130 mein OSPF jeetta hai. Static route background mein wait karta hai aur jaise hi OSPF route withdraw hota hai, install ho jaata hai — yaani automatic backup path milta hai.

options.en: The static route was rejected because 130 is not a valid administrative distance
options.hi: Static route reject ho gaya kyunki 130 valid administrative distance nahi hai

options.en: Only the best source per prefix is installed: OSPF's AD 110 beats the floating static's AD 130, which stays out of the table until the OSPF route is lost
options.hi: Har prefix ke liye sirf best source install hota hai: OSPF ka AD 110 floating static ke AD 130 ko hara deta hai, jo OSPF route jaane tak table se bahar rehta hai

options.en: Static routes to prefixes learned by OSPF must also be redistributed before they appear
options.hi: OSPF se seekhe gaye prefixes ke static routes ko dikhne se pehle redistribute bhi karna padta hai

options.en: The next hop 172.16.1.2 must be a directly connected interface address of R1 itself
options.hi: Next hop 172.16.1.2 khud R1 ke kisi directly connected interface ka address hona chahiye

whyWrong.en: Any AD from 1 to 255 is valid on a static route; 130 is a deliberate, legal choice.
whyWrong.hi: Static route par 1 se 255 tak koi bhi AD valid hai; 130 jaan-boojh kar chuna gaya legal choice hai.

whyWrong.en: Redistribution controls what a protocol advertises to others; it has nothing to do with installing a local static route.
whyWrong.hi: Redistribution yeh control karta hai ki protocol doosron ko kya advertise kare; local static route install karne se iska koi lena-dena nahi.

whyWrong.en: A next hop must be reachable, not directly configured on the router; 172.16.1.2 being a neighbor's address is normal.
whyWrong.hi: Next hop reachable hona chahiye, router par directly configured nahi; 172.16.1.2 ka neighbor ka address hona normal hai.

text.en: Which TWO are advantages of static routing compared with dynamic routing protocols? (Choose two)
text.hi: Dynamic routing protocols ke comparison mein static routing ke kaunse DO advantages hain? (Do choose karo)

explanation.en: Static routes are silent and deterministic: no hello packets, no updates, no protocol computation, and the path is exactly what the administrator typed. The price is manual maintenance — no automatic failover (unless floating statics are pre-built) and configuration workload that grows with every router and prefix.
explanation.hi: Static routes silent aur deterministic hote hain: na hello packets, na updates, na protocol computation, aur path bilkul wahi hota hai jo administrator ne type kiya. Iski keemat hai manual maintenance — koi automatic failover nahi (jab tak floating statics pehle se na bane hon) aur har router aur prefix ke saath configuration ka kaam badhta jaata hai.

options.en: No CPU cycles or link bandwidth are consumed by routing updates
options.hi: Routing updates mein koi CPU cycles ya link bandwidth consume nahi hoti

options.en: Traffic is automatically rerouted when a link fails
options.hi: Link fail hone par traffic automatically reroute hota hai

options.en: The administrator has exact, predictable control over the path traffic takes
options.hi: Administrator ka traffic ke path par exact, predictable control hota hai

options.en: The configuration effort stays small as the network grows
options.hi: Network badhne par bhi configuration effort kam rehta hai

whyWrong.en: Automatic rerouting is precisely what dynamic protocols provide; a static route keeps pointing at a dead path unless it is withdrawn (interface down) or a floating backup exists.
whyWrong.hi: Automatic rerouting hi toh dynamic protocols dete hain; static route dead path ki taraf point karta rehta hai jab tak woh withdraw na ho (interface down) ya floating backup na ho.

whyWrong.en: Scaling is static routing's weakness — every new subnet may require touching many routers by hand.
whyWrong.hi: Scaling static routing ki kamzori hai — har naye subnet ke liye kai routers ko haath se chhoona pad sakta hai.

text.en: Which TWO statements about the command ip route 0.0.0.0 0.0.0.0 192.0.2.1 are true? (Choose two)
text.hi: Command ip route 0.0.0.0 0.0.0.0 192.0.2.1 ke baare mein kaunse DO statements sahi hain? (Do choose karo)

explanation.en: A quad-zero static route has prefix length 0, so under longest-prefix-match it is the last resort — consulted only when nothing else matches. IOS marks it S* (candidate default) and records the gateway of last resort. It stays local: OSPF only advertises a default if default-information originate is configured under the OSPF process.
explanation.hi: Quad-zero static route ki prefix length 0 hoti hai, isliye longest-prefix-match mein yeh last resort hai — sirf tab dekha jaata hai jab kuch aur match na kare. IOS ise S* (candidate default) mark karta hai aur gateway of last resort record karta hai. Yeh local hi rehta hai: OSPF default sirf tab advertise karta hai jab OSPF process ke under default-information originate configure ho.

options.en: The route is used only when no more specific route matches the destination
options.hi: Yeh route sirf tab use hota hai jab koi more specific route destination se match na kare

options.en: The route appears as S* in show ip route and sets the gateway of last resort
options.hi: Yeh route show ip route mein S* ki tarah dikhta hai aur gateway of last resort set karta hai

options.en: The route is automatically advertised to the router's OSPF neighbors
options.hi: Yeh route automatically router ke OSPF neighbors ko advertise hota hai

options.en: The route has an administrative distance of 0
options.hi: Is route ka administrative distance 0 hai

whyWrong.en: Static routes are never advertised automatically; propagating a default into OSPF requires default-information originate (or redistribution).
whyWrong.hi: Static routes kabhi automatically advertise nahi hote; OSPF mein default propagate karne ke liye default-information originate (ya redistribution) chahiye.

whyWrong.en: A static route's default AD is 1; AD 0 is reserved for directly connected routes.
whyWrong.hi: Static route ka default AD 1 hai; AD 0 directly connected routes ke liye reserved hai.

text.en: Match each static route command to the type of route it creates.
text.hi: Har static route command ko us route type se match karo jo woh banata hai.

explanation.en: Recognize static route variants by shape: mask 0.0.0.0 = default route; mask 255.255.255.255 = /32 host route; a trailing number = custom AD, i.e. a floating backup; both an exit interface AND a next hop = fully specified — the preferred form on multi-access links.
explanation.hi: Static route variants ko unki shape se pehchano: mask 0.0.0.0 = default route; mask 255.255.255.255 = /32 host route; end mein ek number = custom AD, yaani floating backup; exit interface AUR next hop dono = fully specified — multi-access links par yahi preferred form hai.

text.en: Type the command that displays only the static routes from the IPv4 routing table.
text.hi: Woh command type karo jo IPv4 routing table se sirf static routes display karta hai.

explanation.en: show ip route accepts a protocol filter: show ip route static lists only S entries, show ip route ospf only O entries, and so on. Handy for confirming that a floating static has (or has not) been installed without scrolling the whole table.
explanation.hi: show ip route ek protocol filter accept karta hai: show ip route static sirf S entries list karta hai, show ip route ospf sirf O entries, waghera. Poori table scroll kiye bina yeh confirm karne ke liye kaam ka hai ki floating static install hua hai (ya nahi).

text.en: Which type of routing protocol is OSPF, and what algorithm does it use to compute best paths?
text.hi: OSPF kis type ka routing protocol hai, aur best paths compute karne ke liye kaunsa algorithm use karta hai?

explanation.en: OSPF is a link-state protocol: every router floods link-state advertisements (LSAs) so that all routers in an area build an identical map (the LSDB), then each router independently runs Dijkstra's SPF algorithm with itself as the root to compute lowest-cost paths.
explanation.hi: OSPF ek link-state protocol hai: har router link-state advertisements (LSAs) flood karta hai taaki area ke saare routers ek identical map (LSDB) bana lein, phir har router independently khud ko root maan kar Dijkstra ka SPF algorithm chalata hai aur lowest-cost paths compute karta hai.

options.en: Distance vector, using the Bellman-Ford algorithm
options.hi: Distance vector, Bellman-Ford algorithm use karta hai

options.en: Link-state, using Dijkstra's shortest path first algorithm
options.hi: Link-state, Dijkstra ka shortest path first algorithm use karta hai

options.en: Path vector, using best-path attributes
options.hi: Path vector, best-path attributes use karta hai

options.en: Hybrid, using the diffusing update algorithm (DUAL)
options.hi: Hybrid, diffusing update algorithm (DUAL) use karta hai

whyWrong.en: Distance vector protocols like RIP learn routes by rumor from neighbors; OSPF builds a full topology map instead.
whyWrong.hi: RIP jaise distance vector protocols neighbors se sun-sunaa kar (by rumor) routes seekhte hain; OSPF iski jagah poora topology map banata hai.

whyWrong.en: Path vector describes BGP, which selects routes using attributes such as AS path.
whyWrong.hi: Path vector BGP ko describe karta hai, jo AS path jaise attributes se routes select karta hai.

whyWrong.en: DUAL is EIGRP's algorithm; EIGRP is the protocol often described as an advanced distance vector or hybrid protocol.
whyWrong.hi: DUAL EIGRP ka algorithm hai; EIGRP ko hi aksar advanced distance vector ya hybrid protocol kaha jaata hai.

text.en: What are the default OSPF hello and dead intervals on a broadcast network such as Ethernet?
text.hi: Ethernet jaise broadcast network par default OSPF hello aur dead intervals kya hain?

explanation.en: On broadcast and point-to-point networks OSPF sends hellos every 10 seconds and declares a neighbor dead after 40 seconds (4x hello) without hearing one. Both values are carried inside the hello packet and MUST match between neighbors, or no adjacency forms.
explanation.hi: Broadcast aur point-to-point networks par OSPF har 10 seconds mein hello bhejta hai aur agar 40 seconds (4x hello) tak hello na sune toh neighbor ko dead declare kar deta hai. Dono values hello packet ke andar carry hoti hain aur neighbors ke beech MATCH honi chahiye, warna adjacency nahi banti.

options.en: Hello 10 seconds, dead 40 seconds
options.hi: Hello 10 seconds, dead 40 seconds

options.en: Hello 30 seconds, dead 120 seconds
options.hi: Hello 30 seconds, dead 120 seconds

options.en: Hello 5 seconds, dead 20 seconds
options.hi: Hello 5 seconds, dead 20 seconds

text.en: To which multicast address does an OSPF router send hello packets so that all OSPF routers on the segment receive them?
text.hi: OSPF router hello packets kis multicast address par bhejta hai taaki segment ke saare OSPF routers unhe receive karein?

explanation.en: 224.0.0.5 is the AllSPFRouters address — every OSPF router listens to it, and hellos are sent there. 224.0.0.6 (AllDRouters) is listened to only by the DR and BDR, so DROTHERs send them updates on that address. OSPF rides directly on IP protocol 89 (no TCP or UDP).
explanation.hi: 224.0.0.5 AllSPFRouters address hai — har OSPF router ise sunta hai, aur hellos yahin bheje jaate hain. 224.0.0.6 (AllDRouters) ko sirf DR aur BDR sunte hain, isliye DROTHERs unhe updates is address par bhejte hain. OSPF seedha IP protocol 89 par chalta hai (na TCP, na UDP).

whyWrong.en: 224.0.0.6 reaches only the DR and BDR; hellos must reach every OSPF router on the link.
whyWrong.hi: 224.0.0.6 sirf DR aur BDR tak pahunchta hai; hellos ko link ke har OSPF router tak pahunchna chahiye.

whyWrong.en: 224.0.0.9 is used by RIPv2.
whyWrong.hi: 224.0.0.9 RIPv2 use karta hai.

whyWrong.en: 224.0.0.18 is used by VRRP.
whyWrong.hi: 224.0.0.18 VRRP use karta hai.

text.en:
A router has no router-id command under its OSPF process. Its interfaces are:

Loopback0            10.255.255.1
Loopback1            172.16.255.1
GigabitEthernet0/0   192.168.100.1
GigabitEthernet0/1   203.0.113.5

Which OSPF router ID does it select?
text.hi:
Ek router ke OSPF process ke under koi router-id command nahi hai. Uske interfaces yeh hain:

Loopback0            10.255.255.1
Loopback1            172.16.255.1
GigabitEthernet0/0   192.168.100.1
GigabitEthernet0/1   203.0.113.5

Woh kaunsa OSPF router ID select karega?

explanation.en: Router ID selection order: (1) manually configured router-id, (2) highest IP address on any up loopback interface, (3) highest IP address on any up physical interface. With no manual ID, the loopbacks are compared and 172.16.255.1 is numerically higher than 10.255.255.1 — physical addresses are never considered while a loopback exists.
explanation.hi: Router ID selection ka order: (1) manually configured router-id, (2) kisi bhi up loopback interface ka highest IP address, (3) kisi bhi up physical interface ka highest IP address. Manual ID nahi hai, toh loopbacks compare hote hain aur 172.16.255.1 numerically 10.255.255.1 se bada hai — jab tak loopback hai, physical addresses consider hi nahi hote.

whyWrong.en: 203.0.113.5 is the highest physical address, but physical interfaces are only consulted when there are no up loopbacks.
whyWrong.hi: 203.0.113.5 highest physical address hai, lekin physical interfaces sirf tab dekhe jaate hain jab koi up loopback na ho.

whyWrong.en: 192.168.100.1 is a physical interface address and is not even the highest one.
whyWrong.hi: 192.168.100.1 ek physical interface address hai aur highest bhi nahi hai.

whyWrong.en: 10.255.255.1 is a loopback, but 172.16.255.1 is numerically higher (172 beats 10 in the first octet).
whyWrong.hi: 10.255.255.1 loopback hai, lekin 172.16.255.1 numerically bada hai (first octet mein 172, 10 se bada hai).

text.en:
On a multi-access Ethernet segment, R1's show ip ospf neighbor displays:

Neighbor ID     Pri   State           Dead Time   Address      Interface
2.2.2.2           1   FULL/DR         00:00:35    10.1.1.2     Gi0/0
3.3.3.3           1   FULL/BDR        00:00:33    10.1.1.3     Gi0/0
4.4.4.4           1   2WAY/DROTHER    00:00:38    10.1.1.4     Gi0/0

Why is the neighbor 4.4.4.4 stuck at 2WAY?
text.hi:
Ek multi-access Ethernet segment par R1 ka show ip ospf neighbor yeh dikhata hai:

Neighbor ID     Pri   State           Dead Time   Address      Interface
2.2.2.2           1   FULL/DR         00:00:35    10.1.1.2     Gi0/0
3.3.3.3           1   FULL/BDR        00:00:33    10.1.1.3     Gi0/0
4.4.4.4           1   2WAY/DROTHER    00:00:38    10.1.1.4     Gi0/0

Neighbor 4.4.4.4 2WAY par kyun atka hua hai?

explanation.en: This output is healthy. On multi-access segments, every router forms FULL adjacencies only with the DR and BDR; pairs of DROTHERs stop at 2-way to avoid a full mesh of adjacencies. R1 shows FULL with the DR (2.2.2.2) and BDR (3.3.3.3), and a normal 2WAY/DROTHER relationship with the other non-designated router.
explanation.hi: Yeh output healthy hai. Multi-access segments par har router FULL adjacency sirf DR aur BDR ke saath banata hai; DROTHERs ke pairs 2-way par ruk jaate hain taaki adjacencies ka full mesh na bane. R1 DR (2.2.2.2) aur BDR (3.3.3.3) ke saath FULL dikhata hai, aur doosre non-designated router ke saath normal 2WAY/DROTHER relationship.

options.en: Its hello parameters do not match R1's
options.hi: Uske hello parameters R1 se match nahi karte

options.en: R1 and 4.4.4.4 are both DROTHERs, and DROTHERs remain in 2-way with each other by design — full adjacency is built only with the DR and BDR
options.hi: R1 aur 4.4.4.4 dono DROTHERs hain, aur DROTHERs design ke hisaab se aapas mein 2-way mein rehte hain — full adjacency sirf DR aur BDR ke saath banti hai

options.en: An MTU mismatch is preventing database synchronization
options.hi: MTU mismatch database synchronization ko rok raha hai

options.en: 4.4.4.4 has failed and is about to be removed from the table
options.hi: 4.4.4.4 fail ho gaya hai aur table se hatne wala hai

whyWrong.en: Mismatched hello parameters would prevent the neighbor from appearing at all — it would never reach 2-way.
whyWrong.hi: Hello parameters mismatch hote toh neighbor dikhta hi nahi — kabhi 2-way tak pahunchta hi nahi.

whyWrong.en: An MTU mismatch shows up as neighbors stuck in EXSTART/EXCHANGE, not resting at 2-way.
whyWrong.hi: MTU mismatch mein neighbors EXSTART/EXCHANGE mein atke dikhte hain, 2-way par aaram se nahi rehte.

whyWrong.en: The dead timer is refreshing normally (38 seconds remaining); nothing indicates a failure.
whyWrong.hi: Dead timer normally refresh ho raha hai (38 seconds baaki); failure ka koi sign nahi hai.

text.en:
Four routers power on simultaneously on a new Ethernet segment:

R1: priority 1,   router ID 1.1.1.1
R2: priority 1,   router ID 10.10.10.10
R3: priority 5,   router ID 2.2.2.2
R4: priority 0,   router ID 99.99.99.99

Which router becomes the DR?
text.hi:
Chaar routers ek naye Ethernet segment par ek saath power on hote hain:

R1: priority 1,   router ID 1.1.1.1
R2: priority 1,   router ID 10.10.10.10
R3: priority 5,   router ID 2.2.2.2
R4: priority 0,   router ID 99.99.99.99

Kaunsa router DR banega?

explanation.en: DR election compares interface priority first — highest wins — and uses the highest router ID only as a tiebreaker. R3's priority 5 beats everyone: R4 is excluded entirely (priority 0 means never participate), and R1/R2 tie at priority 1, where R2's higher RID makes it the BDR. Note the election is not preemptive: once elected, a DR keeps its role.
explanation.hi: DR election pehle interface priority compare karta hai — highest jeetta hai — aur highest router ID sirf tiebreaker hai. R3 ki priority 5 sabko hara deti hai: R4 poori tarah bahar hai (priority 0 matlab kabhi participate nahi karna), aur R1/R2 priority 1 par tie hain, jahan R2 ka higher RID use BDR banata hai. Dhyan do, election preemptive nahi hai: ek baar elect hone ke baad DR apna role rakhta hai.

options.hi: R2

whyWrong.hi: Priority-1 routers mein R1 ka RID sabse kam hai; woh DROTHER banta hai.

whyWrong.en: R2 has the highest router ID, but router ID only breaks priority ties — R3's priority 5 wins first. R2 becomes the BDR.
whyWrong.hi: R2 ka router ID sabse high hai, lekin router ID sirf priority tie todta hai — R3 ki priority 5 pehle jeet jaati hai. R2 BDR banta hai.

whyWrong.hi: Priority 0 R4 ko DR/BDR elections se poori tarah hata deti hai, chahe uska router ID kitna bhi high ho.

text.en: In a single-area OSPF network that has fully converged, what is true about the link-state database (LSDB)?
text.hi: Ek fully converged single-area OSPF network mein link-state database (LSDB) ke baare mein kya sahi hai?

explanation.en: Convergence in link-state routing means LSDB synchronization: every router in the area ends up with the same complete topology map. Each router then runs Dijkstra's SPF independently, placing itself at the root, which is why different routers compute different best paths from the same database.
explanation.hi: Link-state routing mein convergence ka matlab hai LSDB synchronization: area ke har router ke paas same complete topology map hota hai. Phir har router independently Dijkstra ka SPF chalata hai aur khud ko root par rakhta hai, isi wajah se alag-alag routers same database se alag best paths compute karte hain.

options.en: Only the DR maintains the complete LSDB; other routers keep partial copies
options.hi: Sirf DR complete LSDB maintain karta hai; baaki routers partial copies rakhte hain

options.en: Every router in the area holds an identical LSDB and independently runs SPF with itself as the root of the tree
options.hi: Area ke har router ke paas identical LSDB hota hai aur woh independently khud ko tree ka root maan kar SPF chalata hai

options.en: Each router stores only the LSAs that it generated
options.hi: Har router sirf woh LSAs store karta hai jo usne khud generate kiye

options.en: The LSDB and the routing table are the same data structure
options.hi: LSDB aur routing table ek hi data structure hain

whyWrong.en: The DR reduces flooding on a segment but has no monopoly on topology data — all routers hold the full area LSDB.
whyWrong.hi: DR segment par flooding kam karta hai lekin topology data par uski monopoly nahi hai — saare routers poora area LSDB rakhte hain.

whyWrong.en: Routers flood and store all LSAs for the area, not just their own — otherwise SPF could not see the whole topology.
whyWrong.hi: Routers area ke saare LSAs flood aur store karte hain, sirf apne nahi — warna SPF poori topology dekh hi nahi paata.

whyWrong.en: The routing table is the OUTPUT of running SPF over the LSDB; they are distinct structures.
whyWrong.hi: Routing table LSDB par SPF chalane ka OUTPUT hai; dono alag structures hain.

text.en: A segment already has an elected DR and BDR. A new router with interface priority 200 — higher than every existing router — is connected to the segment. What happens?
text.hi: Ek segment par pehle se DR aur BDR elected hain. Interface priority 200 wala ek naya router — jo har existing router se zyada hai — segment se connect kiya jaata hai. Kya hota hai?

explanation.en: OSPF's DR election is non-preemptive: joining routers accept the incumbent DR and BDR regardless of priority. The high-priority newcomer becomes a DROTHER. Its priority 200 only matters at the NEXT election — if the DR fails, the BDR is promoted, and the newcomer would then likely win the BDR election.
explanation.hi: OSPF ka DR election non-preemptive hai: join karne wale routers maujooda DR aur BDR ko accept kar lete hain, priority chahe kuch bhi ho. High-priority naya router DROTHER banta hai. Uski priority 200 sirf AGLE election mein matter karti hai — agar DR fail ho, BDR promote hota hai, aur phir naya router shayad BDR election jeet jaayega.

options.en: The new router immediately becomes the DR and the old DR steps down
options.hi: Naya router turant DR ban jaata hai aur purana DR hat jaata hai

options.en: The existing DR and BDR keep their roles; the new router becomes a DROTHER despite its higher priority
options.hi: Existing DR aur BDR apne roles rakhte hain; naya router higher priority ke bawajood DROTHER banta hai

options.en: A new full election is triggered and all routers restart their adjacencies
options.hi: Ek naya full election trigger hota hai aur saare routers apni adjacencies restart karte hain

options.en: The new router becomes the BDR and waits to be promoted
options.hi: Naya router BDR banta hai aur promote hone ka wait karta hai

whyWrong.en: Unlike HSRP with preemption, OSPF never dethrones a working DR — this avoids constant re-elections and LSA churn.
whyWrong.hi: Preemption wale HSRP ke ulat, OSPF kabhi bhi kaam kar rahe DR ko nahi hatata — isse baar-baar re-elections aur LSA churn se bacha jaata hai.

whyWrong.en: Adjacencies are not reset when a router joins; elections only happen when there is no DR/BDR or one of them fails.
whyWrong.hi: Router join karne par adjacencies reset nahi hoti; election sirf tab hota hai jab DR/BDR na ho ya unmein se koi fail ho.

whyWrong.en: The BDR role is already held; the newcomer does not displace the BDR either, for the same non-preemption reason.
whyWrong.hi: BDR role pehle se kisi ke paas hai; same non-preemption wajah se naya router BDR ko bhi nahi hatata.

text.en: What is the effect of configuring ip ospf priority 0 on a router's Ethernet interface?
text.hi: Router ke Ethernet interface par ip ospf priority 0 configure karne ka kya effect hota hai?

explanation.en: Priority 0 means 'never become DR or BDR' — nothing more. The router still sends hellos, still becomes fully adjacent with the DR and BDR, and still receives all routes. It simply stays a permanent DROTHER, which is useful for routers that should not carry the DR's flooding workload.
explanation.hi: Priority 0 ka matlab hai 'kabhi DR ya BDR nahi banna' — bas itna hi. Router phir bhi hellos bhejta hai, DR aur BDR ke saath fully adjacent hota hai, aur saare routes receive karta hai. Woh bas permanent DROTHER bana rehta hai, jo un routers ke liye useful hai jinhe DR ka flooding workload nahi uthana chahiye.

options.en: The interface stops sending hello packets
options.hi: Interface hello packets bhejna band kar deta hai

options.en: The router is excluded from DR/BDR elections on that segment but still forms a full adjacency with the DR and BDR and exchanges routes normally
options.hi: Router us segment par DR/BDR elections se bahar ho jaata hai, lekin phir bhi DR aur BDR ke saath full adjacency banata hai aur normally routes exchange karta hai

options.en: The router refuses to form any OSPF adjacencies on that interface
options.hi: Router us interface par koi bhi OSPF adjacency banane se mana kar deta hai

options.en: OSPF is disabled on the interface
options.hi: Interface par OSPF disable ho jaata hai

whyWrong.en: Hellos continue; suppressing hellos is what passive-interface does.
whyWrong.hi: Hellos chalte rehte hain; hellos rokna passive-interface ka kaam hai.

whyWrong.en: Adjacencies with the DR and BDR still form and reach FULL; only the election is affected.
whyWrong.hi: DR aur BDR ke saath adjacencies phir bhi banti hain aur FULL tak pahunchti hain; sirf election par asar padta hai.

whyWrong.en: OSPF remains fully operational on the interface — compare with passive-interface or removing the network statement.
whyWrong.hi: Interface par OSPF poori tarah operational rehta hai — passive-interface ya network statement hatane se compare karo.

text.en: During which OSPF neighbor state do routers exchange Database Description (DBD) packets that summarize the contents of their LSDBs?
text.hi: Kis OSPF neighbor state mein routers Database Description (DBD) packets exchange karte hain jo unke LSDBs ke contents ka summary dete hain?

explanation.en: The full state sequence is down, init, 2-way, exstart, exchange, loading, full. In EXSTART the routers elect a master/slave and agree on starting sequence numbers; in EXCHANGE they send the actual DBD summaries; in LOADING each router requests (LSR) and receives (LSU) any LSAs it is missing; FULL means the databases are synchronized.
explanation.hi: Poori state sequence hai down, init, 2-way, exstart, exchange, loading, full. EXSTART mein routers master/slave elect karte hain aur starting sequence numbers par agree karte hain; EXCHANGE mein asli DBD summaries bhejte hain; LOADING mein har router jo LSAs missing hain unhe request (LSR) aur receive (LSU) karta hai; FULL matlab databases synchronized hain.

options.hi: Exstart

options.hi: Exchange

options.en: Loading
options.hi: Loading

options.hi: 2-Way

whyWrong.en: Exstart only negotiates the master/slave relationship and initial sequence numbers that govern the upcoming exchange.
whyWrong.hi: Exstart sirf master/slave relationship aur initial sequence numbers negotiate karta hai jo aane wale exchange ko govern karte hain.

whyWrong.en: Loading is when Link-State Requests are sent for LSAs found missing during the exchange — the DBD summaries have already been sent.
whyWrong.hi: Loading mein exchange ke dauraan missing paaye gaye LSAs ke liye Link-State Requests bheje jaate hain — DBD summaries pehle hi bheje ja chuke hain.

whyWrong.en: 2-Way merely confirms bidirectional hello visibility; no database information has been exchanged yet.
whyWrong.hi: 2-Way sirf bidirectional hello visibility confirm karta hai; abhi tak koi database information exchange nahi hui.

text.en: Which THREE settings must match between two routers on the same link for an OSPF neighbor relationship to form? (Choose three)
text.hi: OSPF neighbor relationship banne ke liye same link par do routers ke beech kaunsi TEEN settings match honi chahiye? (Teen choose karo)

explanation.en: Hello packets carry the area ID, timers, subnet mask, authentication data, and stub flags — all of which must match or the hello is discarded and no neighbor forms. The interfaces must also share a subnet. The process ID is locally significant, and priorities are expected to DIFFER (they drive DR election), so neither needs to match.
explanation.hi: Hello packets area ID, timers, subnet mask, authentication data, aur stub flags carry karte hain — yeh sab match hone chahiye warna hello discard ho jaata hai aur neighbor nahi banta. Interfaces ka same subnet mein hona bhi zaroori hai. Process ID locally significant hai, aur priorities ka ALAG hona expected hai (wahi DR election chalati hain), isliye dono ko match karne ki zaroorat nahi.

whyWrong.en: Priority influences who becomes DR; routers with different priorities form adjacencies without any problem.
whyWrong.hi: Priority yeh decide karti hai ki DR kaun banega; alag priorities wale routers bina kisi problem ke adjacencies banate hain.

text.en: Which TWO statements about DR and BDR behavior on a multi-access segment are true? (Choose two)
text.hi: Multi-access segment par DR aur BDR behavior ke baare mein kaunse DO statements sahi hain? (Do choose karo)

explanation.en: On multi-access networks, full adjacencies are formed only with the DR and BDR (DROTHER pairs stay in 2-way), and the election is non-preemptive — an incumbent DR keeps the role until it fails, no matter who joins later. Priority is the first criterion in elections, with router ID only as tiebreaker, and priority 0 opts a router out entirely.
explanation.hi: Multi-access networks par full adjacencies sirf DR aur BDR ke saath banti hain (DROTHER pairs 2-way mein rehte hain), aur election non-preemptive hai — maujooda DR fail hone tak role rakhta hai, baad mein koi bhi join kare. Elections mein priority pehla criterion hai, router ID sirf tiebreaker, aur priority 0 router ko poori tarah bahar kar deti hai.

options.en: DROTHER routers reach the FULL state only with the DR and BDR
options.hi: DROTHER routers FULL state sirf DR aur BDR ke saath tak pahunchte hain

options.en: A router added later with a higher priority does not take over the DR role
options.hi: Baad mein add kiya gaya higher priority wala router DR role nahi leta

options.en: The router with the highest router ID always becomes DR, regardless of priority
options.hi: Highest router ID wala router hamesha DR banta hai, priority chahe kuch bhi ho

options.en: Setting priority 0 makes a router more likely to win the election
options.hi: Priority 0 set karne se router ke election jeetne ke chances badhte hain

whyWrong.hi: Priority pehle compare hoti hai; highest router ID sirf tab jeetta hai jab priorities tie hon.

whyWrong.en: Priority 0 has the opposite effect — the router never participates in DR/BDR elections.
whyWrong.hi: Priority 0 ka ulta effect hai — router DR/BDR elections mein kabhi participate nahi karta.

text.en: Match each OSPF neighbor state to its meaning.

explanation.en: The progression down, init, 2-way, exstart, exchange, loading, full tells you exactly how far a neighbor relationship got — and where to look when it stalls: stuck in INIT suggests one-way communication, stuck in EXSTART/EXCHANGE suggests an MTU mismatch or duplicate router IDs.
explanation.hi: Progression down, init, 2-way, exstart, exchange, loading, full bilkul batata hai ki neighbor relationship kahan tak pahunchi — aur atakne par kahan dekhna hai: INIT mein atka hai toh one-way communication ka shak, EXSTART/EXCHANGE mein atka hai toh MTU mismatch ya duplicate router IDs ka shak.

right.en: Hello received, but own router ID not yet listed in it
right.hi: Hello receive hua, lekin usmein abhi apna router ID listed nahi hai

right.en: Bidirectional communication confirmed; DR/BDR election can occur
right.hi: Bidirectional communication confirm; DR/BDR election ho sakta hai

right.hi: Master/slave roles aur initial sequence numbers negotiate hote hain
