right.hi: Missing LSAs ke liye Link-State Requests bheje jaate hain

text.en: Which wildcard mask enables OSPF on all interfaces in the 192.168.10.0/24 subnet with the command network 192.168.10.0 ___ area 0?
text.hi: Command network 192.168.10.0 ___ area 0 ke saath kaunsa wildcard mask 192.168.10.0/24 subnet ke saare interfaces par OSPF enable karta hai?

explanation.en: OSPF network statements use wildcard masks — the bit-inverse of the subnet mask. For /24 (255.255.255.0), the wildcard is 0.0.0.255: 0-bits must match exactly, 1-bits are ignored. So any interface whose address starts with 192.168.10 is matched and OSPF is enabled on it.
explanation.hi: OSPF network statements wildcard masks use karte hain — subnet mask ka bit-inverse. /24 (255.255.255.0) ke liye wildcard 0.0.0.255 hai: 0-bits exactly match hone chahiye, 1-bits ignore hote hain. Isliye har woh interface jiska address 192.168.10 se shuru hota hai, match hota hai aur us par OSPF enable ho jaata hai.

whyWrong.en: 255.255.255.0 is the subnet mask; the network command needs its inverse.
whyWrong.hi: 255.255.255.0 subnet mask hai; network command ko iska inverse chahiye.

whyWrong.en: 0.0.255.255 would match any interface beginning with 192.168 — a /16 scope, wider than intended.
whyWrong.hi: 0.0.255.255 har us interface ko match karega jo 192.168 se shuru hota hai — /16 scope, jo intended se zyada wide hai.

whyWrong.en: Wildcard 255.255.255.255 ignores every bit and would match ALL interfaces on the router.
whyWrong.hi: Wildcard 255.255.255.255 har bit ignore karta hai aur router ke SAARE interfaces ko match kar lega.

text.en: R1 is configured with router ospf 1 and R2 with router ospf 5. Their connected interfaces share a subnet, are in area 0, and have matching timers. Will they become OSPF neighbors?
text.hi: R1 par router ospf 1 configure hai aur R2 par router ospf 5. Unke connected interfaces same subnet mein hain, area 0 mein hain, aur timers match karte hain. Kya woh OSPF neighbors banenge?

explanation.en: The number in router ospf N identifies the process on that router only; it is never carried in OSPF packets, so neighbors can use any values. What MUST match: area ID, subnet, hello/dead timers, authentication, and stub flags. Router IDs, in contrast, must be UNIQUE.
explanation.hi: router ospf N ka number sirf us router par process ko identify karta hai; yeh OSPF packets mein kabhi carry nahi hota, isliye neighbors koi bhi values use kar sakte hain. Jo MATCH hona zaroori hai: area ID, subnet, hello/dead timers, authentication, aur stub flags. Iske ulat, router IDs UNIQUE hone chahiye.

options.en: Yes — the process ID is locally significant and does not need to match between routers
options.hi: Haan — process ID locally significant hai aur routers ke beech match hona zaroori nahi

options.en: No — the process IDs must be identical on both routers
options.hi: Nahi — dono routers par process IDs identical hone chahiye

options.en: Only if their router IDs are also identical
options.hi: Sirf tab jab unke router IDs bhi identical hon

options.en: Only after clear ip ospf process is run on both routers
options.hi: Sirf tab jab dono routers par clear ip ospf process chalaya jaaye

whyWrong.en: The process ID never appears in hello packets, so the routers cannot even see each other's value.
whyWrong.hi: Process ID hello packets mein kabhi nahi aata, isliye routers ek doosre ki value dekh bhi nahi sakte.

whyWrong.en: Identical router IDs actually BREAK adjacency — each router must have a unique RID.
whyWrong.hi: Identical router IDs asal mein adjacency TOD dete hain — har router ka RID unique hona chahiye.

whyWrong.en: clear ip ospf process restarts OSPF (for example to apply a new router ID); it is not needed for a normal adjacency.
whyWrong.hi: clear ip ospf process OSPF ko restart karta hai (jaise naya router ID apply karne ke liye); normal adjacency ke liye iski zaroorat nahi.

text.en: Instead of using network statements under the OSPF process, how can an engineer enable OSPF for area 0 directly on interface GigabitEthernet0/0?
text.hi: OSPF process ke under network statements use karne ki jagah, ek engineer interface GigabitEthernet0/0 par directly area 0 ke liye OSPF kaise enable kar sakta hai?

explanation.en: The interface method — ip ospf process-id area area-id — enables OSPF on that specific interface without any network statement. It is more explicit than wildcard matching and is common in modern configurations; both methods can coexist, and the interface command takes precedence for that interface.
explanation.hi: Interface method — ip ospf process-id area area-id — bina kisi network statement ke us specific interface par OSPF enable karta hai. Yeh wildcard matching se zyada explicit hai aur modern configurations mein common hai; dono methods saath mein reh sakte hain, aur us interface ke liye interface command precedence leti hai.

options.en: Apply ip ospf 1 area 0 in interface configuration mode
options.hi: Interface configuration mode mein ip ospf 1 area 0 apply karo

options.en: Apply ospf enable area 0 in interface configuration mode
options.hi: Interface configuration mode mein ospf enable area 0 apply karo

options.en: Apply router ospf 1 area 0 in interface configuration mode
options.hi: Interface configuration mode mein router ospf 1 area 0 apply karo

options.en: Apply network area 0 in interface configuration mode
options.hi: Interface configuration mode mein network area 0 apply karo

whyWrong.en: ospf enable is not valid IOS syntax for OSPFv2.
whyWrong.hi: ospf enable OSPFv2 ke liye valid IOS syntax nahi hai.

whyWrong.en: router ospf 1 is a global configuration command that enters router configuration mode; it is not accepted on an interface.
whyWrong.hi: router ospf 1 ek global configuration command hai jo router configuration mode mein le jaata hai; interface par yeh accept nahi hota.

whyWrong.en: network statements exist only under the router ospf process, and their syntax requires an address and wildcard.
whyWrong.hi: network statements sirf router ospf process ke under hote hain, aur unke syntax mein address aur wildcard zaroori hai.

text.en: An engineer configures passive-interface GigabitEthernet0/2 under router ospf 1. G0/2 connects a user LAN whose subnet is covered by a network statement. What is the result?
text.hi: Ek engineer router ospf 1 ke under passive-interface GigabitEthernet0/2 configure karta hai. G0/2 ek user LAN se connected hai jiska subnet ek network statement se covered hai. Result kya hoga?

explanation.en: Passive-interface is the standard way to handle user-facing LANs: the subnet remains in OSPF (other routers can reach it) while the router stops sending hellos out that port, preventing accidental or malicious adjacencies with devices on the LAN. No neighbors can ever form on a passive interface.
explanation.hi: User-facing LANs ko handle karne ka standard tareeka passive-interface hai: subnet OSPF mein rehta hai (doosre routers usse reach kar sakte hain) jabki router us port se hellos bhejna band kar deta hai, jisse LAN ke devices ke saath galti se ya malicious adjacencies nahi banti. Passive interface par kabhi koi neighbor nahi ban sakta.

options.en: The G0/2 subnet is no longer advertised to other OSPF routers
options.hi: G0/2 subnet ab doosre OSPF routers ko advertise nahi hota

options.en: OSPF stops sending hellos on G0/2 and forms no adjacency there, but the G0/2 subnet is still advertised into OSPF
options.hi: OSPF G0/2 par hellos bhejna band kar deta hai aur wahan koi adjacency nahi banata, lekin G0/2 subnet phir bhi OSPF mein advertise hota hai

options.en: OSPF hellos continue on G0/2 but received routing updates are ignored
options.hi: G0/2 par OSPF hellos chalte rehte hain lekin receive hue routing updates ignore hote hain

options.en: The interface is shut down until passive-interface is removed
options.hi: passive-interface hatne tak interface shut down ho jaata hai

whyWrong.en: Advertising continues — that is the point: include the prefix, silence the protocol chatter.
whyWrong.hi: Advertising chalti rehti hai — yahi toh point hai: prefix include karo, protocol ki chatter band karo.

whyWrong.en: Hellos stop entirely on a passive interface; OSPF does not merely filter received updates.
whyWrong.hi: Passive interface par hellos poori tarah band ho jaate hain; OSPF sirf received updates filter nahi karta.

whyWrong.en: The interface stays up and forwards user traffic normally; only OSPF hello transmission is suppressed.
whyWrong.hi: Interface up rehta hai aur user traffic normally forward karta hai; sirf OSPF hello transmission suppress hota hai.

text.en: After auto-cost reference-bandwidth 10000 is configured under the OSPF process, what is the cost of a 1 Gbps interface?
text.hi: OSPF process ke under auto-cost reference-bandwidth 10000 configure karne ke baad, 1 Gbps interface ki cost kya hogi?

explanation.en: Cost = reference bandwidth / interface bandwidth. The command sets the reference to 10000 Mbps (10 Gbps), so a 1 Gbps interface costs 10000/1000 = 10. This restores differentiation between fast links (with the default 100 Mbps reference, FastEthernet, 1G and 10G all cost 1). Set the same reference bandwidth on EVERY router, or costs become inconsistent and SPF results unpredictable.
explanation.hi: Cost = reference bandwidth / interface bandwidth. Yeh command reference ko 10000 Mbps (10 Gbps) set karta hai, isliye 1 Gbps interface ki cost 10000/1000 = 10 hoti hai. Isse fast links ke beech fark wapas aa jaata hai (default 100 Mbps reference ke saath FastEthernet, 1G aur 10G sab ki cost 1 hoti hai). HAR router par same reference bandwidth set karo, warna costs inconsistent ho jaati hain aur SPF results unpredictable.

whyWrong.en: Cost 1 is what a 1 Gbps interface gets with the DEFAULT reference bandwidth of 100 Mbps (values below 1 round up to 1).
whyWrong.hi: Cost 1 woh hai jo 1 Gbps interface ko DEFAULT reference bandwidth 100 Mbps ke saath milti hai (1 se kam values round up hokar 1 ho jaati hain).

whyWrong.en: 100 would be the new cost of a 100 Mbps FastEthernet interface (10000/100), not of 1 Gbps.
whyWrong.hi: 100, 100 Mbps FastEthernet interface ki nayi cost hogi (10000/100), 1 Gbps ki nahi.

whyWrong.en: 10000 is the reference bandwidth itself, not a resulting interface cost.
whyWrong.hi: 10000 khud reference bandwidth hai, koi resulting interface cost nahi.

text.en:
A router has these interfaces:

GigabitEthernet0/0   10.0.15.1/24
GigabitEthernet0/1   10.10.0.1/24
GigabitEthernet0/2   192.168.10.1/24
Loopback0            10.0.255.254/32

The OSPF process contains only: network 10.0.0.0 0.0.255.255 area 0
On which interfaces is OSPF enabled?
text.hi:
Ek router ke yeh interfaces hain:

GigabitEthernet0/0   10.0.15.1/24
GigabitEthernet0/1   10.10.0.1/24
GigabitEthernet0/2   192.168.10.1/24
Loopback0            10.0.255.254/32

OSPF process mein sirf yeh hai: network 10.0.0.0 0.0.255.255 area 0
Kin interfaces par OSPF enabled hai?

explanation.en: Wildcard 0.0.255.255 requires the first 16 bits to equal 10.0 exactly. G0/0 (10.0.15.1) and Loopback0 (10.0.255.254) both start with 10.0, so they match. G0/1 fails because its second octet is 10, not 0 — a classic misread. 192.168.10.1 does not begin with 10 at all.
explanation.hi: Wildcard 0.0.255.255 ke hisaab se pehle 16 bits exactly 10.0 hone chahiye. G0/0 (10.0.15.1) aur Loopback0 (10.0.255.254) dono 10.0 se shuru hote hain, isliye match karte hain. G0/1 fail hota hai kyunki uska second octet 10 hai, 0 nahi — yeh ek classic galat-padhaai hai. 192.168.10.1 toh 10 se shuru hi nahi hota.

options.en: G0/0 only
options.hi: Sirf G0/0

options.en: G0/0 and Loopback0
options.hi: G0/0 aur Loopback0

options.en: G0/0, G0/1, and Loopback0
options.hi: G0/0, G0/1, aur Loopback0

options.en: All four interfaces
options.hi: Chaaron interfaces

whyWrong.en: Loopback0 also begins with 10.0 and is matched — loopbacks participate in OSPF like any interface.
whyWrong.hi: Loopback0 bhi 10.0 se shuru hota hai aur match hota hai — loopbacks bhi kisi aur interface ki tarah OSPF mein participate karte hain.

whyWrong.en: G0/1 is 10.10.0.1: the second octet (10) does not match the required 0, so the statement does not cover it.
whyWrong.hi: G0/1 10.10.0.1 hai: second octet (10) required 0 se match nahi karta, isliye statement use cover nahi karta.

whyWrong.en: G0/1 and G0/2 both fall outside 10.0.0.0/16, so OSPF is not enabled on them.
whyWrong.hi: G0/1 aur G0/2 dono 10.0.0.0/16 se bahar hain, isliye un par OSPF enable nahi hota.

text.en: R1 connects to R2 over GigabitEthernet. R2 connects to R3 over a 1.544 Mbps T1 serial link. The destination LAN is attached to R3's FastEthernet interface. All routers use the default reference bandwidth (100 Mbps). What is R1's OSPF cost to the destination network?
text.hi: R1, R2 se GigabitEthernet par connected hai. R2, R3 se 1.544 Mbps T1 serial link par connected hai. Destination LAN R3 ke FastEthernet interface se attached hai. Saare routers default reference bandwidth (100 Mbps) use karte hain. Destination network tak R1 ki OSPF cost kya hai?

explanation.en: OSPF cost to a network is the sum of the OUTGOING interface costs along the path, including the interface of the final router that connects to the destination network. GigabitEthernet: 100/1000 rounds up to 1. T1: 100000 kbps / 1544 kbps = 64. Destination FastEthernet: 1. Total = 1 + 64 + 1 = 66.
explanation.hi: Kisi network tak OSPF cost path ke saare OUTGOING interface costs ka sum hoti hai, jismein last router ka woh interface bhi shaamil hai jo destination network se connect karta hai. GigabitEthernet: 100/1000 round up hokar 1. T1: 100000 kbps / 1544 kbps = 64. Destination FastEthernet: 1. Total = 1 + 64 + 1 = 66.

whyWrong.en: 2 counts only the two Ethernet interfaces and ignores the T1's cost of 64 — OSPF is not a hop-count protocol.
whyWrong.hi: 2 sirf do Ethernet interfaces ko count karta hai aur T1 ki cost 64 ko ignore karta hai — OSPF hop-count protocol nahi hai.

whyWrong.en: 65 omits the FastEthernet interface on R3 that attaches the destination network; that stub network's cost is part of the SPF calculation.
whyWrong.hi: 65 mein R3 ka woh FastEthernet interface chhoot gaya jo destination network ko attach karta hai; us stub network ki cost SPF calculation ka hissa hai.

whyWrong.en: 130 roughly doubles the serial cost, as if counting both directions of the T1 — only outgoing interfaces toward the destination are summed.
whyWrong.hi: 130 serial cost ko lagbhag double kar deta hai, jaise T1 ki dono directions count ki hon — sirf destination ki taraf ke outgoing interfaces add hote hain.

text.en: Edge router R1 has a static default route to its ISP and runs OSPF with the internal routers. Which command makes R1 advertise a default route to its OSPF neighbors?
text.hi: Edge router R1 ke paas ISP ki taraf static default route hai aur woh internal routers ke saath OSPF chalata hai. Kaunsa command R1 se uske OSPF neighbors ko default route advertise karwata hai?

explanation.en: default-information originate, configured under router ospf, injects a default route into the OSPF domain — provided R1 itself has a default route installed. Adding the always keyword advertises the default even without one (riskier: R1 could attract traffic it cannot forward). Internal routers then see an external default route via R1.
explanation.hi: router ospf ke under configure kiya gaya default-information originate OSPF domain mein default route inject karta hai — basharte R1 ke paas khud default route installed ho. always keyword add karne se default bina uske bhi advertise hota hai (zyada risky: R1 aisa traffic attract kar sakta hai jise woh forward nahi kar sakta). Phir internal routers R1 ke through ek external default route dekhte hain.

options.en: redistribute static subnets
options.hi: redistribute static subnets

options.en: default-information originate
options.hi: default-information originate

options.en: ip route 0.0.0.0 0.0.0.0 ospf
options.hi: ip route 0.0.0.0 0.0.0.0 ospf

whyWrong.en: Redistributing statics would inject R1's OTHER static prefixes; IOS specifically excludes the default route from redistribution — the default requires default-information originate.
whyWrong.hi: Statics redistribute karne se R1 ke BAAKI static prefixes inject honge; IOS default route ko redistribution se khaas taur par exclude karta hai — default ke liye default-information originate chahiye.

whyWrong.en: The network command only enables OSPF on matching interfaces; it cannot originate a default route.
whyWrong.hi: network command sirf matching interfaces par OSPF enable karta hai; yeh default route originate nahi kar sakta.

whyWrong.en: This is not valid syntax — a static route's next hop must be an IP address or exit interface, not a protocol name.
whyWrong.hi: Yeh valid syntax nahi hai — static route ka next hop IP address ya exit interface hona chahiye, protocol ka naam nahi.

text.en: R1's OSPF router ID is currently 10.0.0.1, derived from a loopback. The design requires the router ID to be 1.1.1.1. Which TWO steps accomplish this? (Choose two)
text.hi: R1 ka OSPF router ID abhi 10.0.0.1 hai, jo ek loopback se aaya hai. Design ke hisaab se router ID 1.1.1.1 hona chahiye. Kaunse DO steps yeh kaam karte hain? (Do choose karo)

explanation.en: Two steps: set the ID explicitly with router-id under the OSPF process, then restart the process (clear ip ospf process, or a reload) because the router ID is chosen only at process start. A manual router-id always outranks loopback and physical addresses in the selection order.
explanation.hi: Do steps: OSPF process ke under router-id se ID explicitly set karo, phir process restart karo (clear ip ospf process, ya reload) kyunki router ID sirf process start par choose hota hai. Selection order mein manual router-id hamesha loopback aur physical addresses se upar hai.

options.en: Configure router-id 1.1.1.1 under router ospf 1
options.hi: router ospf 1 ke under router-id 1.1.1.1 configure karo

options.en: Run clear ip ospf process (or reload the router)
options.hi: clear ip ospf process chalao (ya router reload karo)

options.en: Configure ip ospf router-id 1.1.1.1 on a physical interface
options.hi: Ek physical interface par ip ospf router-id 1.1.1.1 configure karo

options.en: Create a new loopback with 1.1.1.1 — it overrides the current router ID immediately without a restart
options.hi: 1.1.1.1 ke saath naya loopback banao — yeh bina restart ke current router ID ko turant override kar deta hai

whyWrong.en: router-id is a router-configuration-mode command under the OSPF process; there is no per-interface router ID command in OSPFv2.
whyWrong.hi: router-id OSPF process ke under router-configuration-mode command hai; OSPFv2 mein per-interface router ID command nahi hota.

whyWrong.en: Even a higher loopback cannot displace an ALREADY chosen router ID without a process restart — and a manual router-id beats loopbacks anyway.
whyWrong.hi: Higher loopback bhi PEHLE SE chune gaye router ID ko bina process restart ke nahi hata sakta — aur waise bhi manual router-id loopbacks ko hara deta hai.

text.en: Which THREE statements about OSPF interface cost are true? (Choose three)
text.hi: OSPF interface cost ke baare mein kaunse TEEN statements sahi hain? (Teen choose karo)

explanation.en: Cost = reference bandwidth / interface bandwidth, with results below 1 rounded up to 1 — so at the 100 Mbps default, FastEthernet (1) and GigabitEthernet (0.1, rounded to 1) are indistinguishable. Raising the reference bandwidth fixes that, but must be done everywhere for consistent SPF results. ip ospf cost sets an explicit value that wins over the formula.
explanation.hi: Cost = reference bandwidth / interface bandwidth, aur 1 se kam results round up hokar 1 ho jaate hain — isliye 100 Mbps default par FastEthernet (1) aur GigabitEthernet (0.1, round hokar 1) mein fark nahi hota. Reference bandwidth badhane se yeh theek hota hai, lekin consistent SPF results ke liye har jagah karna padta hai. ip ospf cost ek explicit value set karta hai jo formula par jeetti hai.

options.en: With the default reference bandwidth of 100 Mbps, FastEthernet and GigabitEthernet interfaces both end up with cost 1
options.hi: Default reference bandwidth 100 Mbps ke saath FastEthernet aur GigabitEthernet dono interfaces ki cost 1 hoti hai

options.en: If the reference bandwidth is changed, it should be changed identically on every router in the OSPF domain
options.hi: Agar reference bandwidth badla jaaye, toh OSPF domain ke har router par identically badalna chahiye

options.en: The command ip ospf cost overrides the automatically calculated value on that interface
options.hi: Command ip ospf cost us interface par automatically calculated value ko override karta hai

options.en: OSPF cost is calculated from interface load and delay
options.hi: OSPF cost interface load aur delay se calculate hoti hai

options.en: Interfaces with higher bandwidth receive a higher cost
options.hi: Zyada bandwidth wale interfaces ko zyada cost milti hai

whyWrong.en: Load and delay feed EIGRP's composite metric options; OSPF cost is derived purely from bandwidth (or set manually).
whyWrong.hi: Load aur delay EIGRP ke composite metric options mein jaate hain; OSPF cost sirf bandwidth se nikalti hai (ya manually set hoti hai).

whyWrong.en: The relationship is inverse: more bandwidth means a LOWER cost, making the link more attractive to SPF.
whyWrong.hi: Relationship inverse hai: zyada bandwidth matlab KAM cost, jisse link SPF ke liye zyada attractive banta hai.

text.en: Match each OSPF verification command to what it primarily displays.
text.hi: Har OSPF verification command ko us cheez se match karo jo woh mainly display karta hai.

explanation.en: The OSPF troubleshooting quartet: show ip ospf neighbor answers 'who am I adjacent with and how far did we get'; show ip ospf interface exposes the per-link parameters that must match; show ip protocols summarizes the process (RID, networks, passive interfaces); show ip ospf database reveals the topology map itself.
explanation.hi: OSPF troubleshooting ke chaar commands: show ip ospf neighbor batata hai 'main kis-kis ke saath adjacent hoon aur hum kahan tak pahunche'; show ip ospf interface woh per-link parameters dikhata hai jo match hone chahiye; show ip protocols process ka summary deta hai (RID, networks, passive interfaces); show ip ospf database khud topology map dikhata hai.

right.en: Neighbor IDs, adjacency states, and dead timers
right.hi: Neighbor IDs, adjacency states, aur dead timers

right.en: Hello/dead intervals, cost, and DR/BDR per interface
right.hi: Har interface ke Hello/dead intervals, cost, aur DR/BDR

right.en: Router ID, networks being advertised, and passive interfaces
right.hi: Router ID, advertise ho rahe networks, aur passive interfaces

right.en: LSAs stored in the link-state database

text.en: Type the command that lists this router's OSPF neighbors together with their adjacency state and dead timer.
text.hi: Woh command type karo jo is router ke OSPF neighbors ko unki adjacency state aur dead timer ke saath list karta hai.

explanation.en: show ip ospf neighbor is the go-to adjacency check: it shows each neighbor's router ID, priority, state (for example FULL/DR or 2WAY/DROTHER), remaining dead time, interface address, and the local interface — everything needed to confirm or triage an adjacency.
explanation.hi: show ip ospf neighbor adjacency check ke liye go-to command hai: yeh har neighbor ka router ID, priority, state (jaise FULL/DR ya 2WAY/DROTHER), baaki dead time, interface address, aur local interface dikhata hai — adjacency confirm ya triage karne ke liye sab kuch.

text.en: You are in interface configuration mode for GigabitEthernet0/0. Type the command that prevents this router from ever becoming the DR or BDR on that segment.
text.hi: Tum GigabitEthernet0/0 ke interface configuration mode mein ho. Woh command type karo jo is router ko us segment par kabhi DR ya BDR banne se rokta hai.

explanation.en: ip ospf priority 0 removes the interface from DR/BDR elections permanently — the router remains a DROTHER, still forms full adjacencies with the DR and BDR, and still exchanges routes. Values 1-255 instead bias the election upward (default is 1; highest priority wins, router ID breaks ties).
explanation.hi: ip ospf priority 0 interface ko DR/BDR elections se permanently hata deta hai — router DROTHER rehta hai, phir bhi DR aur BDR ke saath full adjacencies banata hai, aur routes exchange karta hai. Values 1-255 election ko upar ki taraf jhukaati hain (default 1 hai; highest priority jeetti hai, router ID tie todta hai).

text.en: In show ip ospf neighbor output, a neighbor is listed as FULL/BDR. What does the FULL state indicate?
text.hi: show ip ospf neighbor output mein ek neighbor FULL/BDR listed hai. FULL state kya batati hai?

explanation.en: FULL is the goal state: both routers have completed database description exchange and LSA loading, so their LSDBs are identical. The /BDR portion tells you the NEIGHBOR's role on that segment — this neighbor is the backup designated router.
explanation.hi: FULL goal state hai: dono routers ne database description exchange aur LSA loading poora kar liya hai, isliye unke LSDBs identical hain. /BDR wala hissa us segment par NEIGHBOR ka role batata hai — yeh neighbor backup designated router hai.

options.en: The neighbor relationship is complete: the two routers' link-state databases are fully synchronized
options.hi: Neighbor relationship complete hai: dono routers ke link-state databases fully synchronized hain

options.en: The neighbor's routing table is full and cannot accept more routes
options.hi: Neighbor ki routing table full hai aur aur routes accept nahi kar sakti

options.en: Hellos are being exchanged but databases have not yet been compared
options.hi: Hellos exchange ho rahe hain lekin databases abhi compare nahi hue

options.en: The neighbor is using its maximum interface bandwidth
options.hi: Neighbor apni maximum interface bandwidth use kar raha hai

whyWrong.en: OSPF neighbor states describe adjacency progress, never routing table capacity.
whyWrong.hi: OSPF neighbor states adjacency ki progress batate hain, routing table capacity kabhi nahi.

whyWrong.en: Hello-only visibility corresponds to 2-WAY; by FULL, the entire database synchronization is finished.
whyWrong.hi: Sirf hello visibility 2-WAY ko represent karti hai; FULL tak poora database synchronization ho chuka hota hai.

whyWrong.en: Neighbor states have nothing to do with link utilization or bandwidth.
whyWrong.hi: Neighbor states ka link utilization ya bandwidth se koi lena-dena nahi.

text.en: R1's G0/0 is configured in OSPF area 0 and R2's directly connected G0/0 is configured in area 1. Both share the subnet and have default timers. What is the result?
text.hi: R1 ka G0/0 OSPF area 0 mein configure hai aur R2 ka directly connected G0/0 area 1 mein. Dono same subnet share karte hain aur default timers hain. Result kya hoga?

explanation.en: The area ID is carried in every hello packet, and a receiving router silently drops hellos whose area does not match the receiving interface's area. The routers never even appear in each other's neighbor tables. Both ends of a link must be placed in the same area.
explanation.hi: Area ID har hello packet mein carry hota hai, aur receive karne wala router chupchaap woh hellos drop kar deta hai jinka area receiving interface ke area se match nahi karta. Routers ek doosre ki neighbor tables mein dikhte bhi nahi. Link ke dono ends same area mein hone chahiye.

options.en: They form an adjacency in area 0, the backbone
options.hi: Woh area 0, yaani backbone, mein adjacency banate hain

options.en: No neighbor relationship forms: each router discards the other's hellos because the area ID does not match
options.hi: Koi neighbor relationship nahi banti: har router doosre ke hellos discard kar deta hai kyunki area ID match nahi karta

options.en: They form an adjacency but exchange only inter-area routes
options.hi: Woh adjacency banate hain lekin sirf inter-area routes exchange karte hain

options.en: They remain stuck in the EXSTART state
options.hi: Woh EXSTART state mein atke rehte hain

whyWrong.en: There is no negotiation or fallback to the backbone; mismatched areas simply mean the hellos are rejected.
whyWrong.hi: Backbone par koi negotiation ya fallback nahi hota; mismatched areas ka matlab bas itna hai ki hellos reject ho jaate hain.

whyWrong.en: Inter-area routing happens through Area Border Routers that legitimately sit in both areas — not through a mismatched link.
whyWrong.hi: Inter-area routing Area Border Routers ke through hoti hai jo legitimately dono areas mein hote hain — mismatched link ke through nahi.

whyWrong.en: EXSTART problems (like MTU mismatches) occur AFTER a neighbor is discovered; an area mismatch prevents discovery entirely.
whyWrong.hi: EXSTART problems (jaise MTU mismatch) neighbor discover hone ke BAAD aati hain; area mismatch discovery hi nahi hone deta.

text.en:
R1 and R2 share an Ethernet link but never become neighbors. show ip ospf interface g0/0 shows:

R1:  Timer intervals configured, Hello 10, Dead 40
R2:  Timer intervals configured, Hello 30, Dead 120

What is the cause?
text.hi:
R1 aur R2 ek Ethernet link share karte hain lekin kabhi neighbors nahi bante. show ip ospf interface g0/0 yeh dikhata hai:

R1:  Timer intervals configured, Hello 10, Dead 40
R2:  Timer intervals configured, Hello 30, Dead 120

Cause kya hai?

explanation.en: Hello and dead intervals are carried in the hello packet and must match exactly between neighbors on the link; a mismatch makes each side ignore the other's hellos, so the neighbor never appears. R2's 30/120 values look like NBMA defaults — fix with ip ospf hello-interval 10 (dead adjusts to 40) or match the values manually on both sides.
explanation.hi: Hello aur dead intervals hello packet mein carry hote hain aur link par neighbors ke beech exactly match hone chahiye; mismatch hone par dono side ek doosre ke hellos ignore karte hain, isliye neighbor kabhi dikhta hi nahi. R2 ki 30/120 values NBMA defaults jaisi lagti hain — ip ospf hello-interval 10 se fix karo (dead apne aap 40 ho jaata hai) ya dono sides par values manually match karo.

options.en: The hello and dead intervals do not match, so each router discards the other's hellos
options.hi: Hello aur dead intervals match nahi karte, isliye har router doosre ke hellos discard kar deta hai

options.en: R2's timers exceed the maximum allowed on Ethernet
options.hi: R2 ke timers Ethernet par allowed maximum se zyada hain

options.en: R1 is sending hellos three times faster, overwhelming R2
options.hi: R1 teen guna tezi se hellos bhej raha hai, jisse R2 overwhelm ho raha hai

options.en: The dead interval must equal the hello interval for an adjacency to form
options.hi: Adjacency banne ke liye dead interval hello interval ke barabar hona chahiye

whyWrong.en: 30/120 are perfectly legal values (they are the NBMA defaults); the problem is only that they differ from R1's.
whyWrong.hi: 30/120 bilkul legal values hain (yeh NBMA defaults hain); problem sirf yeh hai ki yeh R1 se alag hain.

whyWrong.en: Hello rate does not overwhelm anything at these timescales; the packets are discarded due to the parameter mismatch, not the rate.
whyWrong.hi: In timescales par hello rate kuch overwhelm nahi karta; packets parameter mismatch ki wajah se discard hote hain, rate ki wajah se nahi.

whyWrong.en: The dead interval is normally FOUR times the hello interval; the requirement is that both routers use the same pair of values.
whyWrong.hi: Dead interval normally hello interval ka CHAAR guna hota hai; requirement yeh hai ki dono routers same pair of values use karein.

text.en: R1 shows a neighbor stuck in the INIT state for several minutes. What does this indicate?
text.hi: R1 par ek neighbor kai minutes se INIT state mein atka dikh raha hai. Iska kya matlab hai?

explanation.en: INIT means 'I hear you, but you do not hear me': R1 received a hello from R2 that does not list R1's router ID as a seen neighbor. Communication is one-way — a classic symptom of an inbound ACL on R2 blocking OSPF (IP protocol 89) or multicast 224.0.0.5, or a Layer 1/2 problem in one direction. Healthy adjacencies pass through INIT in moments.
explanation.hi: INIT ka matlab hai 'main tumhe sun raha hoon, lekin tum mujhe nahi sun rahe': R1 ko R2 se ek hello mila jismein R1 ka router ID seen neighbor ki tarah listed nahi hai. Communication one-way hai — iska classic symptom hai R2 par inbound ACL jo OSPF (IP protocol 89) ya multicast 224.0.0.5 ko block kar raha ho, ya ek direction mein Layer 1/2 problem. Healthy adjacencies INIT se pal bhar mein nikal jaati hain.

options.en: One-way communication: R1 receives R2's hellos, but R2 is not receiving (or not listing) R1's hellos — R1's router ID never appears in R2's hello packets
options.hi: One-way communication: R1 ko R2 ke hellos mil rahe hain, lekin R2 ko R1 ke hellos nahi mil rahe (ya woh unhe list nahi kar raha) — R1 ka router ID R2 ke hello packets mein kabhi nahi aata

options.en: The routers are waiting for the DR election to complete
options.hi: Routers DR election poora hone ka wait kar rahe hain

options.en: R1 and R2 have mismatched hello timers
options.hi: R1 aur R2 ke hello timers mismatched hain

options.en: Database synchronization is in progress and will complete shortly
options.hi: Database synchronization chal raha hai aur jaldi poora ho jaayega

whyWrong.en: The DR election happens at 2-WAY; stuck in INIT means the relationship has not even become bidirectional.
whyWrong.hi: DR election 2-WAY par hota hai; INIT mein atkne ka matlab hai relationship abhi bidirectional bhi nahi hui.

whyWrong.en: Mismatched timers cause hellos to be discarded entirely — the neighbor would not appear in the table at all, not sit in INIT.
whyWrong.hi: Mismatched timers mein hellos poori tarah discard ho jaate hain — neighbor table mein dikhta hi nahi, INIT mein nahi baithta.

whyWrong.en: Database exchange happens in EXSTART/EXCHANGE/LOADING, which come after 2-WAY.
whyWrong.hi: Database exchange EXSTART/EXCHANGE/LOADING mein hota hai, jo 2-WAY ke baad aate hain.

text.en: R1 and R2 cycle between EXSTART and EXCHANGE and never reach FULL. R1's interface MTU is 1500 and R2's is 9000. Which action fixes the adjacency?
text.hi: R1 aur R2 EXSTART aur EXCHANGE ke beech ghoomte rehte hain aur kabhi FULL tak nahi pahunchte. R1 ka interface MTU 1500 hai aur R2 ka 9000. Kaunsa action adjacency fix karta hai?

explanation.en: The interface MTU is advertised in Database Description packets, and a mismatch makes routers refuse to synchronize — the classic stuck-in-EXSTART/EXCHANGE symptom. Align the MTUs (best) or apply ip ospf mtu-ignore on the interface to suppress the check (a workaround that risks dropping large LSAs).
explanation.hi: Interface MTU Database Description packets mein advertise hota hai, aur mismatch hone par routers synchronize karne se mana kar dete hain — yahi classic stuck-in-EXSTART/EXCHANGE symptom hai. MTUs align karo (best) ya check suppress karne ke liye interface par ip ospf mtu-ignore apply karo (ek workaround jismein bade LSAs drop hone ka risk hai).

options.en: Configure matching MTU values on both interfaces (or configure ip ospf mtu-ignore)
options.hi: Dono interfaces par matching MTU values configure karo (ya ip ospf mtu-ignore configure karo)

options.en: Increase the dead interval on both routers
options.hi: Dono routers par dead interval badhao

options.en: Configure identical OSPF process IDs
options.hi: Identical OSPF process IDs configure karo

options.en: Set both interface priorities to the same value
options.hi: Dono interface priorities same value par set karo

whyWrong.en: Timers already match — the routers found each other and got past 2-WAY; timers are not the blocker here.
whyWrong.hi: Timers pehle se match karte hain — routers ne ek doosre ko dhoondh liya aur 2-WAY se aage nikal gaye; yahan timers blocker nahi hain.

whyWrong.en: Process IDs are locally significant and play no role in adjacency formation.
whyWrong.hi: Process IDs locally significant hain aur adjacency banne mein koi role nahi rakhte.

whyWrong.en: Priorities affect only DR/BDR election, which already happened at 2-WAY; they do not block database exchange.
whyWrong.hi: Priorities sirf DR/BDR election ko affect karti hain, jo 2-WAY par pehle hi ho chuka; yeh database exchange ko block nahi karti.

text.en:
R1 forms no adjacency with R2 on G0/1, although the subnet appears correctly in R2's routing table via OSPF. On R1, show ip protocols includes:

Routing Protocol is "ospf 1"
  Router ID 1.1.1.1
  Passive Interface(s):
    GigabitEthernet0/1

What is the problem and the fix?
text.hi:
R1, G0/1 par R2 ke saath koi adjacency nahi banata, halaanki subnet R2 ki routing table mein OSPF ke through sahi dikh raha hai. R1 par show ip protocols mein yeh hai:

Routing Protocol is "ospf 1"
  Router ID 1.1.1.1
  Passive Interface(s):
    GigabitEthernet0/1

Problem kya hai aur fix kya hai?

explanation.en: A passive interface never sends hellos, so no adjacency can form on it — while the interface's subnet is still advertised into OSPF, which is exactly why R2 has the route but no neighbor. Remove the passive setting for that interface (or move the link out of any passive-interface default policy) to bring the adjacency up.
explanation.hi: Passive interface kabhi hellos nahi bhejta, isliye us par koi adjacency nahi ban sakti — jabki interface ka subnet phir bhi OSPF mein advertise hota hai, isi wajah se R2 ke paas route hai lekin neighbor nahi. Adjacency up karne ke liye us interface ki passive setting hatao (ya link ko kisi bhi passive-interface default policy se bahar karo).

options.en: G0/1 is passive, so R1 sends no hellos on it; configure no passive-interface GigabitEthernet0/1 under router ospf 1
options.hi: G0/1 passive hai, isliye R1 us par koi hellos nahi bhejta; router ospf 1 ke under no passive-interface GigabitEthernet0/1 configure karo

options.en: The router ID is invalid; configure a router ID matching the interface address
options.hi: Router ID invalid hai; interface address se match karta router ID configure karo

options.en: OSPF is not enabled on G0/1; add a network statement for its subnet
options.hi: G0/1 par OSPF enabled nahi hai; uske subnet ke liye network statement add karo

options.en: R2 must also configure a passive interface for symmetry
options.hi: Symmetry ke liye R2 par bhi passive interface configure karna padega

whyWrong.en: 1.1.1.1 is a perfectly valid router ID; router IDs need not match any interface address.
whyWrong.hi: 1.1.1.1 bilkul valid router ID hai; router IDs ka kisi interface address se match hona zaroori nahi.

whyWrong.en: OSPF IS enabled on G0/1 — that is why its subnet is being advertised; the interface is merely passive.
whyWrong.hi: G0/1 par OSPF enabled HAI — isi wajah se uska subnet advertise ho raha hai; interface bas passive hai.

whyWrong.en: Passive interfaces suppress adjacencies; making R2 passive too would just guarantee the adjacency never forms.
whyWrong.hi: Passive interfaces adjacencies suppress karte hain; R2 ko bhi passive banane se bas yeh pakka ho jaayega ki adjacency kabhi na bane.

text.en: Two routers on the same segment both use OSPF router ID 1.1.1.1, and the log shows %OSPF-4-DUP_RTRID_NBR messages. What is the impact and the correct fix?
text.hi: Same segment par do routers dono OSPF router ID 1.1.1.1 use karte hain, aur log mein %OSPF-4-DUP_RTRID_NBR messages dikhte hain. Impact kya hai aur sahi fix kya hai?

explanation.en: Router IDs must be unique in the OSPF domain: a router ignores neighbors claiming its own RID, and duplicate RIDs elsewhere in the network cause LSAs to overwrite each other and routes to flap. Assign a unique router-id under one router's OSPF process and apply it with clear ip ospf process.
explanation.hi: OSPF domain mein router IDs unique hone chahiye: router un neighbors ko ignore karta hai jo uska apna RID claim karte hain, aur network mein kahin aur duplicate RIDs hone se LSAs ek doosre ko overwrite karte hain aur routes flap karte hain. Ek router ke OSPF process ke under unique router-id assign karo aur clear ip ospf process se apply karo.

options.en: They cannot form an adjacency with each other; configure a unique router-id on one of them and restart its OSPF process
options.hi: Woh aapas mein adjacency nahi bana sakte; unmein se ek par unique router-id configure karo aur uska OSPF process restart karo

options.en: They form an adjacency but load-balance all traffic; no action is needed
options.hi: Woh adjacency banate hain lekin saara traffic load-balance karte hain; koi action ki zaroorat nahi

options.en: One router automatically increments its router ID; wait for reconvergence
options.hi: Ek router apna router ID automatically increment kar leta hai; reconvergence ka wait karo

options.en: The DR election fails for the whole segment until both routers are removed
options.hi: Dono routers hatne tak poore segment ka DR election fail ho jaata hai

whyWrong.en: No adjacency forms between duplicates — and even distant duplicates corrupt the LSDB view; this always requires action.
whyWrong.hi: Duplicates ke beech koi adjacency nahi banti — aur door ke duplicates bhi LSDB view ko corrupt karte hain; isme hamesha action chahiye.

whyWrong.en: IOS never changes a router ID by itself; the duplicate persists until an administrator intervenes.
whyWrong.hi: IOS kabhi khud se router ID nahi badalta; administrator ke intervene karne tak duplicate bana rehta hai.

whyWrong.en: Other routers on the segment can still elect a DR; the duplication specifically breaks the relationship between (and LSAs of) the two offenders.
whyWrong.hi: Segment ke doosre routers phir bhi DR elect kar sakte hain; duplication khaas taur par un do offenders ke beech ka relationship (aur unke LSAs) todta hai.

text.en:
R1 and R2 are cabled directly and both have OSPF enabled on the link, but they never appear in each other's neighbor tables:

R1 G0/0:  ip address 10.1.12.1 255.255.255.0
R2 G0/0:  ip address 10.1.12.130 255.255.255.128

What is the cause?
text.hi:
R1 aur R2 directly cabled hain aur dono ne link par OSPF enable kiya hai, lekin woh kabhi ek doosre ki neighbor tables mein nahi dikhte:

R1 G0/0:  ip address 10.1.12.1 255.255.255.0
R2 G0/0:  ip address 10.1.12.130 255.255.255.128

Cause kya hai?

explanation.en: OSPF hellos on multi-access networks carry the network mask, and a receiving router discards hellos whose subnet/mask do not match its own interface. R2 lives in 10.1.12.128/25; from R2's view, R1's 10.1.12.1 is not even in its subnet — and the masks differ besides. Re-address so both interfaces share one subnet and mask.
explanation.hi: Multi-access networks par OSPF hellos network mask carry karte hain, aur receive karne wala router woh hellos discard kar deta hai jinka subnet/mask uske apne interface se match nahi karta. R2 10.1.12.128/25 mein hai; R2 ki nazar se R1 ka 10.1.12.1 uske subnet mein hai hi nahi — aur upar se masks bhi alag hain. Re-address karo taaki dono interfaces ek hi subnet aur mask share karein.

options.en: The interfaces are not in the same subnet, and their masks differ: R1 expects 10.1.12.0/24 while R2 is in 10.1.12.128/25 — the hello subnet check fails
options.hi: Interfaces same subnet mein nahi hain, aur unke masks alag hain: R1 10.1.12.0/24 expect karta hai jabki R2 10.1.12.128/25 mein hai — hello subnet check fail hota hai

options.en: R2's address is a broadcast address and cannot be used
options.hi: R2 ka address broadcast address hai aur use nahi ho sakta

options.en: OSPF requires a /30 or /31 mask on point-to-point Ethernet links
options.hi: OSPF ko point-to-point Ethernet links par /30 ya /31 mask chahiye

options.en: R1's address is too low in the range to form an adjacency
options.hi: R1 ka address range mein bahut neeche hai isliye adjacency nahi ban sakti

whyWrong.en: The broadcast address of 10.1.12.128/25 is 10.1.12.255; .130 is a valid host address in that subnet.
whyWrong.hi: 10.1.12.128/25 ka broadcast address 10.1.12.255 hai; .130 us subnet ka valid host address hai.

whyWrong.en: Any mask works on Ethernet as long as BOTH ends agree; /30 and /31 are merely common for point-to-point addressing efficiency.
whyWrong.hi: Ethernet par koi bhi mask chalta hai jab tak DONO ends agree karein; /30 aur /31 sirf point-to-point addressing efficiency ke liye common hain.

whyWrong.en: Host address values within a subnet are irrelevant to adjacency; only subnet membership and matching parameters matter.
whyWrong.hi: Subnet ke andar host address ki value adjacency ke liye irrelevant hai; sirf subnet membership aur matching parameters matter karte hain.

text.en: R1's link to R2 is configured with ip ospf authentication message-digest and a matching key command, but R2 has no OSPF authentication configured at all. What is the result?
text.hi: R1 ka R2 ki taraf wala link ip ospf authentication message-digest aur ek matching key command ke saath configure hai, lekin R2 par koi OSPF authentication configure hi nahi hai. Result kya hoga?

explanation.en: Authentication type (none, plaintext, or MD5/message-digest) and the key itself are both checked on every OSPF packet. R1 requires MD5 while R2 sends unauthenticated packets, so each side discards the other's hellos and the neighbor never appears. Configure the same authentication mode and key on BOTH ends of the link.
explanation.hi: Authentication type (none, plaintext, ya MD5/message-digest) aur key dono har OSPF packet par check hote hain. R1 ko MD5 chahiye jabki R2 unauthenticated packets bhejta hai, isliye dono side ek doosre ke hellos discard karte hain aur neighbor kabhi dikhta nahi. Link ke DONO ends par same authentication mode aur key configure karo.

options.en: No neighbor relationship forms: each router rejects the other's OSPF packets because the authentication type does not match
options.hi: Koi neighbor relationship nahi banti: har router doosre ke OSPF packets reject karta hai kyunki authentication type match nahi karta

options.en: The adjacency forms but all routes are marked as untrusted
options.hi: Adjacency banti hai lekin saare routes untrusted mark hote hain

options.en: R2 automatically learns the MD5 key from R1's hellos
options.hi: R2 automatically R1 ke hellos se MD5 key seekh leta hai

options.en: The routers fall back to plaintext authentication
options.hi: Routers plaintext authentication par fall back kar jaate hain

whyWrong.en: There is no 'untrusted route' state in OSPF; authentication failure is binary — packets are simply discarded.
whyWrong.hi: OSPF mein koi 'untrusted route' state nahi hoti; authentication failure binary hai — packets bas discard ho jaate hain.

whyWrong.en: Keys are never transmitted in a learnable form; MD5 sends only a hash, and configuration must be done manually on each router.
whyWrong.hi: Keys kabhi seekhne laayak form mein transmit nahi hoti; MD5 sirf hash bhejta hai, aur configuration har router par manually karni padti hai.

whyWrong.en: OSPF never negotiates authentication downward; a type mismatch is a hard failure, not a fallback trigger.
whyWrong.hi: OSPF kabhi authentication ko neeche negotiate nahi karta; type mismatch ek hard failure hai, fallback ka trigger nahi.

text.en: Two OSPF routers discover each other but remain stuck in the EXSTART state. Which TWO are likely causes? (Choose two)
text.hi: Do OSPF routers ek doosre ko discover kar lete hain lekin EXSTART state mein atke rehte hain. Kaunse DO likely causes hain? (Do choose karo)

explanation.en: EXSTART is where DBD exchange begins, and two classic failures live there: an MTU mismatch (advertised in DBD packets and rejected by the peer) and duplicate router IDs (master/slave negotiation cannot resolve when both claim the same ID). Both require reaching the neighbor stage first — which mismatched hellos would have prevented entirely.
explanation.hi: EXSTART woh jagah hai jahan DBD exchange shuru hota hai, aur do classic failures yahin hote hain: MTU mismatch (DBD packets mein advertise hota hai aur peer reject kar deta hai) aur duplicate router IDs (jab dono same ID claim karein toh master/slave negotiation resolve nahi hoti). Dono ke liye pehle neighbor stage tak pahunchna zaroori hai — jo mismatched hellos poori tarah rok dete.

options.en: Mismatched interface MTU values
options.hi: Mismatched interface MTU values

options.en: Both routers are using the same router ID
options.hi: Dono routers same router ID use kar rahe hain

options.en: Mismatched hello intervals
options.hi: Mismatched hello intervals

options.en: Both interfaces have priority 0
options.hi: Dono interfaces ki priority 0 hai

whyWrong.en: Mismatched hello timers cause hellos to be discarded, so the routers would never appear in each other's neighbor tables — they could not reach EXSTART.
whyWrong.hi: Mismatched hello timers mein hellos discard ho jaate hain, isliye routers ek doosre ki neighbor tables mein dikhte hi nahi — EXSTART tak pahunch hi nahi sakte the.

whyWrong.en: With every router at priority 0 no DR can be elected, which strands neighbors at 2-WAY on a broadcast network — not at EXSTART.
whyWrong.hi: Har router priority 0 par ho toh koi DR elect nahi ho sakta, jisse broadcast network par neighbors 2-WAY par atak jaate hain — EXSTART par nahi.

text.en: R1 should form an OSPF adjacency with R2 across G0/0, but show ip ospf neighbor on R1 is empty. Which THREE are possible causes? (Choose three)
text.hi: R1 ko G0/0 ke across R2 ke saath OSPF adjacency banani chahiye, lekin R1 par show ip ospf neighbor khaali hai. Kaunse TEEN possible causes hain? (Teen choose karo)

explanation.en: An empty neighbor table means hellos are not being exchanged or are being rejected. Passive interfaces send no hellos; ACLs can silently drop OSPF (protocol 89) or its multicast destination; and mismatched timers make receivers discard otherwise healthy hellos. Also check area IDs, subnets/masks, and authentication — the full mismatch checklist.
explanation.hi: Khaali neighbor table ka matlab hai ki hellos exchange nahi ho rahe ya reject ho rahe hain. Passive interfaces koi hellos nahi bhejte; ACLs chupchaap OSPF (protocol 89) ya uske multicast destination ko drop kar sakte hain; aur mismatched timers receivers se waise theek hellos bhi discard karwa dete hain. Area IDs, subnets/masks, aur authentication bhi check karo — poori mismatch checklist.

options.en: G0/0 is configured as a passive interface
options.hi: G0/0 passive interface ki tarah configure hai

options.en: An inbound ACL on the link blocks IP protocol 89 or multicast 224.0.0.5
options.hi: Link par ek inbound ACL IP protocol 89 ya multicast 224.0.0.5 ko block karta hai

options.en: The hello and dead intervals differ between R1 and R2
options.hi: R1 aur R2 ke beech hello aur dead intervals alag hain

options.en: R1 and R2 use different OSPF process IDs
options.hi: R1 aur R2 alag OSPF process IDs use karte hain

options.en: R2 has a higher router ID than R1
options.hi: R2 ka router ID R1 se zyada hai

whyWrong.en: Process IDs are locally significant; R1 using process 1 and R2 using process 7 has no effect on adjacency.
whyWrong.hi: Process IDs locally significant hain; R1 ka process 1 aur R2 ka process 7 use karna adjacency par koi asar nahi daalta.

whyWrong.en: Router ID values only influence DR/BDR elections; a higher or lower RID never prevents neighbor formation (only DUPLICATE RIDs do).
whyWrong.hi: Router ID values sirf DR/BDR elections ko influence karti hain; higher ya lower RID kabhi neighbor banne se nahi rokta (sirf DUPLICATE RIDs rokte hain).

text.en: Type the command that displays the OSPF hello and dead intervals, cost, state, and DR/BDR for each OSPF-enabled interface.
text.hi: Woh command type karo jo har OSPF-enabled interface ke liye OSPF hello aur dead intervals, cost, state, aur DR/BDR display karta hai.

explanation.en: show ip ospf interface is the fastest way to compare the parameters that must match between neighbors: hello and dead intervals, area, network type, and authentication, plus this router's cost, priority, and the segment's DR/BDR. Run it on both routers and diff the values when an adjacency will not form.
explanation.hi: show ip ospf interface un parameters ko compare karne ka sabse tez tareeka hai jo neighbors ke beech match hone chahiye: hello aur dead intervals, area, network type, aur authentication, saath mein is router ki cost, priority, aur segment ka DR/BDR. Jab adjacency na bane, dono routers par chalao aur values ka diff karo.

text.en: What problem do first-hop redundancy protocols such as HSRP solve?
text.hi: HSRP jaise first-hop redundancy protocols kaunsi problem solve karte hain?

explanation.en: Hosts are configured with a single default gateway address and cannot detect a dead router. An FHRP creates a virtual IP (and virtual MAC) that hosts use as their gateway; the routers in the group decide among themselves who actively forwards for it, and another takes over transparently if the active router fails.
explanation.hi: Hosts par ek hi default gateway address configure hota hai aur woh dead router detect nahi kar sakte. FHRP ek virtual IP (aur virtual MAC) banata hai jise hosts apne gateway ki tarah use karte hain; group ke routers aapas mein decide karte hain ki uske liye actively kaun forward karega, aur agar active router fail ho toh doosra transparently take over kar leta hai.

options.en: They let two or more routers share a virtual IP and MAC address, so hosts keep a working default gateway even if one router fails
options.hi: Yeh do ya zyada routers ko ek virtual IP aur MAC address share karne dete hain, taaki ek router fail hone par bhi hosts ka default gateway kaam karta rahe

options.en: They load-balance user traffic across multiple internet service providers
options.hi: Yeh user traffic ko multiple internet service providers ke beech load-balance karte hain

options.en: They prevent Layer 2 loops between redundant switches
options.hi: Yeh redundant switches ke beech Layer 2 loops rokte hain

options.en: They encrypt traffic between hosts and their default gateway
options.hi: Yeh hosts aur unke default gateway ke beech traffic encrypt karte hain

whyWrong.en: ISP load balancing is a routing/BGP design matter; FHRPs operate between gateway routers and hosts on a LAN.
whyWrong.hi: ISP load balancing ek routing/BGP design ka matter hai; FHRPs LAN par gateway routers aur hosts ke beech kaam karte hain.

whyWrong.en: Loop prevention is Spanning Tree Protocol's job, at Layer 2.
whyWrong.hi: Loop prevention Layer 2 par Spanning Tree Protocol ka kaam hai.

whyWrong.en: FHRPs provide availability, not confidentiality — no user traffic is encrypted.
whyWrong.hi: FHRPs availability dete hain, confidentiality nahi — koi user traffic encrypt nahi hota.

text.en: What is the default HSRP priority on a Cisco router?
text.hi: Cisco router par default HSRP priority kya hai?

explanation.en: HSRP priority defaults to 100 and ranges 0-255; the router with the highest priority becomes active, and to guarantee a specific router wins you raise it (commonly to 110 or 150) with standby group priority value. Remember that a higher-priority router only takes over an existing active router if preemption is configured.
explanation.hi: HSRP priority ka default 100 hai aur range 0-255 hai; sabse high priority wala router active banta hai, aur kisi specific router ko jitaane ke liye tum use standby group priority value se badhate ho (aam taur par 110 ya 150). Yaad rakho, higher-priority router existing active router ko sirf tab hatata hai jab preemption configured ho.

whyWrong.en: 1 is the default OSPF interface priority — a common mix-up between the two protocols.
whyWrong.hi: 1 default OSPF interface priority hai — dono protocols ke beech common confusion.

whyWrong.en: 110 is a common CONFIGURED value to win the election (and OSPF's AD), but not the default.
whyWrong.hi: 110 election jeetne ke liye aksar CONFIGURE ki jaane wali value hai (aur OSPF ka AD), lekin default nahi.

whyWrong.en: 255 is the maximum configurable priority, not the default.
whyWrong.hi: 255 maximum configurable priority hai, default nahi.

text.en: Two routers in HSRP group 1 boot at the same time. Both use the default priority of 100. R1's interface IP is 10.1.1.1 and R2's is 10.1.1.2. Which router becomes active, and why?
text.hi: HSRP group 1 ke do routers ek saath boot hote hain. Dono default priority 100 use karte hain. R1 ka interface IP 10.1.1.1 hai aur R2 ka 10.1.1.2. Kaunsa router active banega, aur kyun?

explanation.en: HSRP elects the active router by highest priority; when priorities tie, the highest interface IP address in the group wins the tiebreak. With both at the default 100, R2's 10.1.1.2 beats R1's 10.1.1.1, so R2 becomes active and R1 becomes standby.
explanation.hi: HSRP active router highest priority se elect karta hai; jab priorities tie hon, toh group mein highest interface IP address tiebreak jeetta hai. Dono default 100 par hain, isliye R2 ka 10.1.1.2 R1 ke 10.1.1.1 ko hara deta hai, R2 active banta hai aur R1 standby.

options.en: R1, because lower IP addresses are preferred
options.hi: R1, kyunki lower IP addresses prefer hote hain

options.en: R2, because with equal priorities the highest interface IP address wins the election
options.hi: R2, kyunki equal priorities par highest interface IP address election jeetta hai

options.en: R1, because it appears first in the configuration
options.hi: R1, kyunki woh configuration mein pehle aata hai

options.en: Neither — the group stays down until an administrator sets different priorities
options.hi: Koi nahi — jab tak administrator alag priorities set na kare, group down rehta hai

whyWrong.en: The tiebreak favors the HIGHEST IP address, not the lowest.
whyWrong.hi: Tiebreak HIGHEST IP address ko favor karta hai, lowest ko nahi.

whyWrong.en: Configuration order on different devices has no meaning to the election; only priority and IP address are compared.
whyWrong.hi: Alag devices par configuration order ka election ke liye koi matlab nahi; sirf priority aur IP address compare hote hain.

whyWrong.en: Equal priorities are perfectly workable — the IP tiebreaker guarantees a deterministic winner.
whyWrong.hi: Equal priorities se bilkul kaam chalta hai — IP tiebreaker ek deterministic winner pakka karta hai.

text.en: What virtual MAC address does HSRP version 1 use for group 10?
text.hi: HSRP version 1 group 10 ke liye kaunsa virtual MAC address use karta hai?

explanation.en: HSRPv1 virtual MACs follow 0000.0c07.acXX, where XX is the group number in HEX. Group 10 decimal = 0x0A, giving 0000.0c07.ac0a. Hosts ARP for the virtual IP and receive this virtual MAC, so whichever router is active answers to it — a failover never requires hosts to update their ARP caches.
explanation.hi: HSRPv1 virtual MACs 0000.0c07.acXX follow karte hain, jahan XX group number HEX mein hai. Group 10 decimal = 0x0A, toh 0000.0c07.ac0a milta hai. Hosts virtual IP ke liye ARP karte hain aur yeh virtual MAC paate hain, isliye jo bhi router active hai woh isse answer karta hai — failover par hosts ko apne ARP caches update karne ki zaroorat nahi padti.

whyWrong.en: This reads the group number as decimal: ac10 would actually be group 16 (0x10).
whyWrong.hi: Yeh group number ko decimal ki tarah padhta hai: ac10 asal mein group 16 (0x10) hoga.

whyWrong.en: 0000.0c9f.fXXX is the HSRP VERSION 2 format, which carries the group number in its last three hex digits.
whyWrong.hi: 0000.0c9f.fXXX HSRP VERSION 2 ka format hai, jo group number ko apne last teen hex digits mein carry karta hai.

whyWrong.en: 0000.5e00.01XX is the VRRP virtual MAC format.
whyWrong.hi: 0000.5e00.01XX VRRP virtual MAC format hai.

text.en: R1 (priority 150) was the HSRP active router until it lost power; R2 (priority 100) took over as active. R1 later comes back online with its configuration intact, which does not include the preempt command. Which router is active now?
text.hi: R1 (priority 150) HSRP active router tha jab tak uski power nahi gayi; R2 (priority 100) ne active ki tarah take over kiya. Baad mein R1 apni configuration ke saath wapas online aata hai, jismein preempt command nahi hai. Ab kaunsa router active hai?

explanation.en: HSRP preemption is OFF by default: an active router keeps its role until it fails, even when a higher-priority router is available. R1 therefore returns as standby. To let the higher-priority router reclaim the active role automatically, configure standby group preempt on R1.
explanation.hi: HSRP preemption by default OFF hota hai: active router fail hone tak apna role rakhta hai, chahe higher-priority router available ho. Isliye R1 standby ki tarah wapas aata hai. Higher-priority router ko active role automatically wapas lene dene ke liye R1 par standby group preempt configure karo.

options.en: R1, because its priority of 150 is higher
options.hi: R1, kyunki uski priority 150 zyada hai

options.en: R2 — it remains active because preemption is disabled by default, so R1 waits in standby despite its higher priority
options.hi: R2 — woh active rehta hai kyunki preemption by default disabled hai, isliye R1 higher priority ke bawajood standby mein wait karta hai

options.en: R1, because a previously active router always resumes its role
options.hi: R1, kyunki pehle active raha router hamesha apna role wapas leta hai

options.en: Neither — both routers become active and share the load
options.hi: Koi nahi — dono routers active ban jaate hain aur load share karte hain

whyWrong.en: Priority only decides elections when no active router exists — or when the higher-priority router has preemption enabled.
whyWrong.hi: Priority sirf tab election decide karti hai jab koi active router na ho — ya jab higher-priority router par preemption enabled ho.

whyWrong.en: HSRP has no memory of past roles; without preemption, incumbency wins.
whyWrong.hi: HSRP ko purane roles yaad nahi rehte; preemption ke bina jo pehle se active hai wahi jeetta hai.

whyWrong.en: Two active routers in one group would be a malfunction (usually a communication failure between them), not normal behavior.
whyWrong.hi: Ek group mein do active routers ek malfunction hoga (aam taur par unke beech communication failure), normal behavior nahi.

text.en: Which pair of interface commands configures HSRP group 1 with virtual IP 10.1.1.254 and makes this router prefer the active role with priority 110?
text.hi: Interface commands ka kaunsa pair HSRP group 1 ko virtual IP 10.1.1.254 ke saath configure karta hai aur is router ko priority 110 ke saath active role prefer karwata hai?

explanation.en: Classic IOS HSRP configuration uses the standby keyword on the interface: standby 1 ip 10.1.1.254 defines the group and virtual IP, and standby 1 priority 110 raises this router above the default 100. Add standby 1 preempt if it should take the active role back from a lower-priority incumbent.
explanation.hi: Classic IOS HSRP configuration interface par standby keyword use karti hai: standby 1 ip 10.1.1.254 group aur virtual IP define karta hai, aur standby 1 priority 110 is router ko default 100 se upar le jaata hai. Agar ise kam priority wale maujooda router se active role wapas lena hai toh standby 1 preempt add karo.

options.en: standby 1 ip 10.1.1.254 and standby 1 priority 110
options.hi: standby 1 ip 10.1.1.254 aur standby 1 priority 110

options.en: hsrp 1 ip 10.1.1.254 and hsrp 1 priority 110
options.hi: hsrp 1 ip 10.1.1.254 aur hsrp 1 priority 110

options.en: standby 1 virtual-ip 10.1.1.254 and standby 1 priority 110
options.hi: standby 1 virtual-ip 10.1.1.254 aur standby 1 priority 110

options.en: standby ip 10.1.1.254 group 1 and standby priority 110 group 1
options.hi: standby ip 10.1.1.254 group 1 aur standby priority 110 group 1

whyWrong.en: hsrp is not the configuration keyword in classic IOS — the commands all begin with standby.
whyWrong.hi: Classic IOS mein hsrp configuration keyword nahi hai — saare commands standby se shuru hote hain.

whyWrong.en: The keyword is simply ip, not virtual-ip: standby 1 ip address.
whyWrong.hi: Keyword sirf ip hai, virtual-ip nahi: standby 1 ip address.

whyWrong.en: The group number comes immediately after standby, not in a trailing group clause.
whyWrong.hi: Group number standby ke turant baad aata hai, end mein group clause mein nahi.

text.en: Which statement correctly contrasts VRRP with HSRP?
text.hi: Kaunsa statement VRRP aur HSRP ka sahi contrast batata hai?

explanation.en: VRRP (RFC-standardized) uses master/backup roles, multicast 224.0.0.18, virtual MAC 0000.5e00.01XX — and preempts by default, so the highest-priority router takes over automatically. HSRP and GLBP are Cisco proprietary; HSRP's active/standby election does NOT preempt unless configured, and GLBP adds per-host load balancing via multiple forwarders.
explanation.hi: VRRP (RFC-standardized) master/backup roles, multicast 224.0.0.18, virtual MAC 0000.5e00.01XX use karta hai — aur by default preempt karta hai, isliye highest-priority router automatically take over karta hai. HSRP aur GLBP Cisco proprietary hain; HSRP ka active/standby election configure kiye bina preempt NAHI karta, aur GLBP multiple forwarders ke through per-host load balancing add karta hai.

options.en: VRRP is an IETF open standard whose preemption is enabled by default, whereas HSRP is Cisco proprietary with preemption disabled by default
options.hi: VRRP ek IETF open standard hai jiska preemption by default enabled hai, jabki HSRP Cisco proprietary hai aur uska preemption by default disabled hai

options.en: VRRP is Cisco proprietary, while HSRP is the industry standard
options.hi: VRRP Cisco proprietary hai, jabki HSRP industry standard hai

options.en: HSRP enables preemption by default, while VRRP requires it to be configured
options.hi: HSRP by default preemption enable karta hai, jabki VRRP mein ise configure karna padta hai

options.en: GLBP and VRRP are both open standards supported by all vendors
options.hi: GLBP aur VRRP dono open standards hain jo saare vendors support karte hain

whyWrong.en: It is exactly reversed: HSRP is the Cisco-proprietary protocol and VRRP is the open standard.
whyWrong.hi: Bilkul ulta hai: HSRP Cisco-proprietary protocol hai aur VRRP open standard.

whyWrong.en: Also reversed — preemption is default-on in VRRP and default-off in HSRP.
whyWrong.hi: Yeh bhi ulta hai — preemption VRRP mein default-on hai aur HSRP mein default-off.

whyWrong.en: GLBP is Cisco proprietary; only VRRP among the two is an open standard.
whyWrong.hi: GLBP Cisco proprietary hai; in dono mein sirf VRRP open standard hai.

text.en: Which TWO statements about a two-router HSRP group are true? (Choose two)
text.hi: Do-router HSRP group ke baare mein kaunse DO statements sahi hain? (Do choose karo)

explanation.en: The whole design centers on the virtual identity: hosts point their default gateway at the virtual IP, hosts resolve it to the virtual MAC, and the active router alone answers for that MAC while the standby monitors hellos, ready to take over. Within one HSRP group there is no load sharing (that is GLBP's feature, or achieved with multiple HSRP groups per VLAN).
explanation.hi: Poora design virtual identity par based hai: hosts apna default gateway virtual IP par point karte hain, use virtual MAC mein resolve karte hain, aur sirf active router us MAC ke liye answer karta hai jabki standby hellos monitor karta hai, take over karne ke liye tayyar. Ek HSRP group ke andar koi load sharing nahi hoti (woh GLBP ka feature hai, ya har VLAN mein multiple HSRP groups se hoti hai).

options.en: Hosts on the LAN use the virtual IP address as their default gateway
options.hi: LAN ke hosts virtual IP address ko apne default gateway ki tarah use karte hain

options.en: Only the active router forwards traffic sent to the virtual MAC address
options.hi: Virtual MAC address par bheja gaya traffic sirf active router forward karta hai

options.en: The active and standby routers load-share traffic for the group by default
options.hi: Active aur standby routers by default group ka traffic load-share karte hain

options.en: The virtual IP address must be identical to the active router's physical interface address
options.hi: Virtual IP address active router ke physical interface address ke identical hona chahiye

whyWrong.en: A single HSRP group is strictly active/standby; load balancing requires GLBP or running multiple HSRP groups with different active routers.
whyWrong.hi: Ek single HSRP group strictly active/standby hota hai; load balancing ke liye GLBP chahiye ya alag active routers ke saath multiple HSRP groups chalane padte hain.

whyWrong.en: The virtual IP must be a separate, unused address in the same subnet — distinct from every physical interface address.
whyWrong.hi: Virtual IP same subnet ka ek alag, unused address hona chahiye — har physical interface address se alag.

text.en:
Two routers are configured on the same LAN:

R1 interface G0/0:
  standby 1 ip 10.1.1.254
  standby 1 priority 120

R2 interface G0/0:
  standby 1 ip 10.1.1.254
  standby 1 preempt

Which TWO statements are true? (Choose two)
text.hi:
Same LAN par do routers aise configure hain:

R1 interface G0/0:
  standby 1 ip 10.1.1.254
  standby 1 priority 120

R2 interface G0/0:
  standby 1 ip 10.1.1.254
  standby 1 preempt

Kaunse DO statements sahi hain? (Do choose karo)

explanation.en: At simultaneous boot, the election compares priorities: R1's 120 beats R2's default 100, so R1 is active. When R1 later dies, R2 takes over — and KEEPS the role when R1 returns, because preemption must be configured on the RECOVERING higher-priority router (R1), and it is not. R2's preempt only matters if R2 ever has the higher priority.
explanation.hi: Ek saath boot hone par election priorities compare karta hai: R1 ka 120 R2 ke default 100 ko hara deta hai, isliye R1 active hai. Jab baad mein R1 down hota hai, R2 take over karta hai — aur R1 ke wapas aane par bhi role RAKHTA hai, kyunki preemption RECOVER hone wale higher-priority router (R1) par configure honi chahiye, aur woh nahi hai. R2 ka preempt sirf tab matter karta hai jab kabhi R2 ki priority zyada ho.

options.en: If both routers boot at the same time, R1 becomes active because its priority (120) beats R2's default 100
options.hi: Agar dono routers ek saath boot hon, toh R1 active banta hai kyunki uski priority (120) R2 ke default 100 ko hara deti hai

options.en: If R1 fails and later recovers, R2 stays active because R1 does not have preemption configured
options.hi: Agar R1 fail hokar baad mein recover ho, toh R2 active rehta hai kyunki R1 par preemption configured nahi hai

options.en: R2 will seize the active role from a healthy R1 because R2 has preempt configured
options.hi: R2 healthy R1 se active role chheen lega kyunki R2 par preempt configured hai

options.en: The group uses virtual MAC address 0000.0c07.ac10
options.hi: Group virtual MAC address 0000.0c07.ac10 use karta hai

whyWrong.en: Preemption lets a router take over only when its priority is HIGHER than the current active router's; R2's 100 never beats a healthy R1 at 120.
whyWrong.hi: Preemption router ko sirf tab take over karne deta hai jab uski priority current active router se ZYADA ho; R2 ka 100 kabhi bhi 120 wale healthy R1 ko nahi harata.

whyWrong.en: Group 1 in HSRPv1 maps to virtual MAC 0000.0c07.ac01 — the group number is expressed in hex as the last octet, so ac10 would be group 16.
whyWrong.hi: HSRPv1 mein group 1 virtual MAC 0000.0c07.ac01 par map hota hai — group number last octet mein hex mein likha jaata hai, isliye ac10 group 16 hoga.

text.en: Match each HSRP state to its meaning.
text.hi: Har HSRP state ko uske matlab se match karo.

explanation.en: The HSRP state ladder is init, learn, listen, speak, standby, active. A router climbs from learning the virtual IP, through listening to hellos, to speaking in elections; each group ends up with exactly one active forwarder and one standby, while any additional routers remain in listen.
explanation.hi: HSRP state ladder hai init, learn, listen, speak, standby, active. Router virtual IP seekhne se shuru karke, hellos sunne se hote hue, elections mein bolne tak upar chadhta hai; har group mein exactly ek active forwarder aur ek standby hota hai, jabki baaki routers listen mein rehte hain.

right.en: Waiting to learn the virtual IP address from the active router
right.hi: Active router se virtual IP address seekhne ka wait kar raha hai

right.en: Knows the virtual IP; monitors hellos but is neither active nor standby
right.hi: Virtual IP pata hai; hellos monitor karta hai lekin na active hai na standby

right.en: Sends hellos and participates in the active/standby election
right.hi: Hellos bhejta hai aur active/standby election mein participate karta hai

right.en: Next in line; takes over if the active router fails
right.hi: Line mein agla; active router fail hone par take over karta hai

right.en: Currently forwards packets sent to the virtual MAC address
right.hi: Abhi virtual MAC address par bheje gaye packets forward karta hai

text.en: Type the command that displays a one-line-per-group summary of HSRP status, including this router's state, the active and standby routers, and the virtual IP.
text.hi: Woh command type karo jo HSRP status ka har group ke liye ek-line summary dikhata hai, jismein is router ki state, active aur standby routers, aur virtual IP shaamil hain.

explanation.en: show standby brief compresses HSRP status into one line per group: interface, group number, local priority, P flag if preemption is enabled, local state, and the addresses of the active router, standby router, and virtual IP. Use plain show standby for full detail including timers and the virtual MAC.
explanation.hi: show standby brief HSRP status ko har group ke liye ek line mein compress karta hai: interface, group number, local priority, preemption enabled ho toh P flag, local state, aur active router, standby router aur virtual IP ke addresses. Timers aur virtual MAC samet poori detail ke liye plain show standby use karo.
